name: Aam Panna

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Achari Aloo (Pickled Five-Spice Tangy Baby Potatoes)

ingredients.name: Baby potatoes (or cubed potatoes), boiled and halved
Achari masala (fennel, mustard, nigella, fenugreek & cumin seeds, coarsely crushed)
Turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli & amchur (dry mango powder)

steps.section: Crack achari spices in smoking mustard oil
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until smoking, cool slightly, and crackle dry red chillies, hing, and the coarsely crushed achari five-spice blend.
Add halved boiled potatoes, ginger, turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli, amchur, and salt; toss on medium flame for 10-12 minutes until crusted and tangy.

notes: Bold, tangy pickle-spiced potatoes great with poori, paratha, or dal-chawal.

name: Ajwain Paratha (Carom Seed Layered Flaky Paratha)

steps.text: Knead soft wheat dough. Roll into a circle, brush with ghee, sprinkle crushed ajwain and salt, fold into a square or triangle, and roll out.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp golden blisters appear. Serve with masala chai or pickle.

notes: Digestive, aromatic everyday Indian breakfast paratha.

name: Aloo Baingan Masala (Homestyle Potato & Brinjal Curry)

ingredients.name: Panch phoron or cumin seeds & hing
Turmeric, coriander, red chilli & amchur/garam masala

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with panch phoron/cumin and hing, and fry cubed potatoes for 4 minutes before adding cubed brinjal.
Add ginger, chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, red chilli powder, and salt; cover and cook on medium-low heat until soft and jammy.

notes: Comforting homestyle sabzi that pairs with both roti and dal-rice.

name: Aloo Beans Bhaja (Crispy French Beans & Potato Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Green French beans, trimmed and cut into 1.5-inch pieces
Nigella seeds (kalo jeere) or cumin seeds & garlic

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella/cumin seeds and green chillies, and fry potato strips for 4 minutes.
Add French beans, turmeric, cumin powder, and salt; cook covered for 5 minutes, then uncover and stir-fry with black pepper until crisp-tender.

notes: Quick everyday dry side dish for lunchboxes and weekday meals.

name: Aloo Bhaja

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Bharta (Potato Mash)

ingredients.name: Dry red chilli (shukno lonka) or green chilli

steps.text: Wash and boil the potatoes until fork-tender, then drain, cool slightly, and peel off the skins.
Heat mustard oil until smoking, fry dry red chillies until crisp, and crush them with a pinch of salt. Optionally lightly sauté half of the chopped onion.
Mash the warm potatoes smoothly with crushed chillies, raw or fried onion, green chilli, fresh coriander leaves, salt, and raw mustard oil. Serve warm with steamed rice and dal.

notes: Using pungent kachi ghani mustard oil and a mix of raw and lightly fried onions gives authentic Bengali Aloo Bharta flavour.

name: Aloo Bhindi Masala (Crispy Okra & Potato Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Okra (bhindi), wiped dry and cut into 1-inch pieces
Turmeric, coriander, red chilli & amchur powder

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle cumin and ajwain, and fry potato wedges until golden and 75% tender.
Add okra pieces and sliced onion; cook uncovered on medium flame with turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder for 8 minutes, then season with salt and amchur at the end.

notes: Adding salt and amchur at the very end keeps the okra crisp and non-slimy.

name: Aloo Bori Jhol (Bengali Sun-Dried Lentil Dumpling & Potato Light Broth)

ingredients.name: Bengali urad/moong dal bori (sun-dried lentil dumplings)

steps.text: Fry the sun-dried lentil dumplings (bori) in hot mustard oil until golden brown and remove immediately.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, fry potato wedges with ginger paste, cumin powder, turmeric, and tomato, then add warm water and cook until potatoes are soft.
Drop in the fried boris, simmer for 3 minutes until they soften slightly while keeping a bite, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Soothing, light Bengali summer lunch jhol.

name: Aloo Chingri Kalia (Bengali Prawn & Potato Kalia)

ingredients.name: Whole garam masala, Kashmiri chilli, cumin & salt

steps.text: Marinate prawns and potatoes with turmeric and salt. Lightly fry prawns for 2 minutes; fry potatoes until golden brown.
Temper mustard oil with whole garam masala and bay leaf. Fry onions, then add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, whisked yogurt, and spices until oil separates.
Add potatoes and warm water; simmer until potatoes soften, then add prawns and cook for 5 minutes. Finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: A richer, festive version of prawn potato curry ideal for Sunday lunches and special occasions.

name: Aloo Chokha (Bihari Spiced Potato Bharta)

ingredients.name: Green chillies & roasted dry red chilli

steps.text: Boil potatoes until soft, peel, and mash while warm so no large lumps remain.
Roast dry red chillies and garlic cloves over a direct flame or in a dry pan until aromatic, then crush coarsely.
Fold finely chopped onion, crushed garlic-chilli, green chillies, coriander, lemon juice, salt, and raw mustard oil into the mashed potatoes.

notes: Pairs classically with dal-chawal, khichdi, or litti.

name: Aloo Chorchori (Bengali Mustard-Seasoned Potato Baton Medley)

steps.text: Temper mustard oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies; add potato batons, chopped tomato, turmeric, and salt, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add warm water, cover and cook until potatoes are soft, then stir in mustard paste and simmer for 4 minutes until semi-dry. Finish with coriander and raw mustard oil.

notes: Tangy, pungent Bengali mustard potato chorchori.

name: Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Jhuri (Crisp Potato Matchsticks & Crumbled Fish Egg Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander & salt

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, and fry potato matchsticks with a pinch of turmeric until golden and tender-crisp.
Push potatoes aside, add sliced onion, green chillies, and mashed fish eggs with salt and chilli powder, and stir-fry until the roe turns crumbly.
Mix the crisp potatoes and golden fish roe granules together and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Great side dish alongside masoor dal and steamed rice.

name: Aloo Gobi Adraki (Dry Spiced Ginger Potato & Cauliflower Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger juliennes & slit green chillies
Cumin seeds, turmeric, coriander, red chilli, amchur & garam masala

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle cumin seeds, and pan-roast potato wedges and cauliflower florets on medium-high flame for 6 minutes until lightly browned.
Add chopped onion, ginger juliennes, green chillies, turmeric, coriander, red chilli powder, and salt; cover on low heat (no water) until tender-crisp.
Add chopped tomato, amchur, garam masala, and kasuri methi; toss uncovered for 3 minutes.

notes: Cooking without water keeps the cauliflower florets firm and flavorful.

ingredients.name: Cumin, coriander, turmeric & Bengali bhaja masala
Bay leaf, dry red chilli, hing, sugar & salt

steps.text: Temper mustard oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and hing; fry cubed potatoes and chopped onion until golden.
Add ginger paste, chopped tomato, cumin, coriander, and turmeric; cook until pulpy.
Add boiled kabuli chana and warm water; simmer for 9 minutes, lightly mashing a few potatoes, and finish with roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Hearty accompaniment to luchi, radhaballabhi, or pitai paratha.

name: Aloo Masala Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Aloo Matar (Homestyle Spiced Potato & Green Peas Curry)

ingredients.name: Cumin, coriander, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli & garam masala

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, brown chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook tomato puree and spice powders until oil separates.
Add cubed potatoes, green peas, salt, and warm water; cover and simmer for 12 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, and chopped coriander leaves.

notes: Comforting everyday curry for roti, paratha, poori, or jeera rice.

name: Aloo Methi (Fresh Fenugreek Leaves & Crispy Potato Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
Fresh methi (fenugreek) leaves, washed and finely chopped
Garlic cloves (chopped) & whole dry red chillies
Cumin seeds, hing, turmeric & coriander powder

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with cumin seeds, hing, chopped garlic, and dry red chillies, and fry cubed potatoes with turmeric until golden and 80% cooked.
Add chopped fenugreek leaves, coriander powder, and salt; stir-fry uncovered on medium-low heat for 6 minutes until the methi wilts and coats the potatoes.

notes: Cooking uncovered after adding methi prevents the leaves from turning bitter.

name: Aloo Palak (Potatoes in Spiced Garlic Spinach Gravy)

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves, finely chopped & green chillies
Cumin seeds, turmeric, coriander & garam masala

steps.text: Pan-fry cubed potatoes in oil with a pinch of salt and turmeric until golden and tender; set aside.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and chopped garlic, fry chopped onion and tomato with spices until soft.
Stir in the blanched spinach puree and fried potatoes, simmer gently for 5 minutes, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Nutritious spinach and potato curry great with phulkas or steamed rice.

name: Aloo Paratha (Homestyle)

steps.text: Mix flour and salt; add water gradually and knead to a soft dough. Rest covered.
Divide into portions and roll or shape according to the bread style.
Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Peyajkoli Bhaja (Winter Spring Onion Stalks & Potato Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Onion flower stalks (peyajkoli), cut into 1.5-inch pieces

steps.text: Temper mustard oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies; fry potato strips with turmeric for 4 minutes.
Add onion flower stalks and salt; stir-fry on medium heat for 7-8 minutes until tender-crisp and lightly charred.

notes: Winter staple in Bengali homes.

name: Aloo Phulkopi Dalna (Bengali Roasted Cauliflower & Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Roasted cumin powder, coriander, turmeric & chilli powder
Bay leaf, whole garam masala, cumin seeds, sugar & salt

steps.text: Fry cauliflower florets and potato wedges in mustard oil until golden-brown spots appear; set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, and cumin seeds; cook ginger paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders until fragrant.
Add roasted potatoes, cauliflower, green peas, and warm water; simmer until tender and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: Pairs equally well with steamed rice, luchi, or radhaballabhi.

name: Aloo Potol Dalna (Bengali Pointed Gourd & Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Pointed gourd (potol / parwal), scraped and halved
Cumin, coriander, turmeric & Kashmiri red chilli powder
Bay leaf, whole cumin, garam masala, sugar & salt

steps.text: Fry scraped pointed gourd halves and potato wedges in mustard oil with a pinch of turmeric and salt until golden brown; remove.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders until oil separates.
Return fried potol and potatoes with warm water, salt, and a pinch of sugar; simmer covered until tender and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: One of the most beloved everyday and festive Bengali vegetable curries.

name: Aloo Potol Diye Macher Dimer Borar Jhol (Pointed Gourd, Potato & Fish Egg Fritter Curry)

ingredients.name: Pointed gourd (potol / parwal), scraped and halved
Bay leaf, cumin seeds, cumin-coriander powder, turmeric, garam masala & salt

steps.section: Fry fish egg boras, potol and potatoes
steps.text: Make small boras from fish eggs, chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry in mustard oil. Fry potol halves and potato wedges until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, chopped tomato, turmeric, and cumin-coriander powder.
Add fried potatoes, potol, and warm water; simmer until tender, then add the fish roe boras for the final 4 minutes and finish with garam masala.

notes: Wholesome Bengali summer lunch curry.

name: Aloo Puri (Mashed Potato & Spice Kneaded Crispy Poori)

ingredients.name: Whole wheat flour (atta) & 2 tbsp fine sooji
Potatoes, boiled and finely grated (no lumps)
Carom seeds (ajwain), kasuri methi, turmeric, chilli flakes & cumin powder

steps.text: Mix finely grated boiled potatoes, wheat flour, sooji, ajwain, kasuri methi, coriander, spices, and salt; knead into a firm dough using minimal water.
Roll oiled dough balls into small discs and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden brown.

notes: So flavorful they can be eaten on their own with curd, pickle, or chai.

name: Aloo Shimla Mirch (Potato & Capsicum Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Green bell peppers (shimla mirch / capsicum), cubed
Turmeric, coriander, red chilli, amchur & garam masala

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, and cook cubed potatoes with turmeric and salt covered until nearly tender.
Add cubed bell peppers, chopped tomato, coriander powder, chilli powder, and amchur; stir-fry for 5-6 minutes so the capsicum retains a slight crunch.

notes: Flavorful tiffin sabzi that pairs wonderfully with parathas.

name: Aloo Soyabean Kosha (Bengali Soya Chunks & Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Soya chunks (meal maker), boiled and squeezed
Cumin, coriander, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli & garam masala

steps.text: Boil soya chunks in salted water, squeeze dry, and pan-fry in mustard oil with turmeric alongside potato cubes until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, brown chopped onions, and roast ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes, soya chunks, and warm water; simmer covered for 7 minutes until tender and finish with garam masala.

notes: High-protein homestyle Bengali soya-potato curry.

name: Aloo Tikki

Bitter gourd (uchhe / korola), thinly sliced into rounds

steps.text: Toss thinly sliced bitter gourd and potatoes with salt and turmeric powder.
Heat mustard oil in a wide skillet and fry the slices on medium heat until crisp and golden brown.

notes: Classic Bengali first-course lunch accompaniment eaten with plain hot rice and ghee.

name: Aloor Chokka (Bengali Spiced Potato & Black Chickpea Curry)

ingredients.name: Soaked & boiled kala chana (black chickpeas) or grated coconut
Panch phoron, bay leaf & dry red chilli
Cumin, coriander, turmeric & bhaja masala powder

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and panch phoron, and fry cubed potatoes for 4-5 minutes until lightly golden.
Add ginger paste, chopped tomato, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; sauté until tomatoes soften.

steps.section: Simmer with chana and bhaja masala
steps.text: Add boiled kala chana and warm water; cover and cook until potatoes are tender and gravy is thick. Finish with sugar and roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Classic Bengali winter and festive side dish for luchi, porota, or khichuri.

name: Americano

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Amritsari Aloo Kulcha (Crispy Spiced Potato Stuffed Kulcha)

ingredients.name: Onion, ginger, green chillies & coriander leaves, finely chopped
Crushed coriander seeds, anardana (pomegranate seed) powder / amchur & red chilli
Yogurt, baking powder & butter (for layering and basting)

steps.text: Knead flour with yogurt, baking powder, salt, and water; roll out, spread softened butter, fold like an envelope, and rest for 20 minutes so the crust bakes flaky.
Mix mashed potatoes with chopped onion, green chillies, coriander, crushed coriander seeds, and anardana/amchur. Stuff inside the laminated dough, top with coriander leaves, and roll oval.
Cook on a hot iron tawa (or bake at 220°C) until crisp and blistered, then slather generously with butter.

notes: Laminating the dough with butter gives Amritsari Kulcha its signature flaky crunch.

name: Andhra Royyala Iguru (Spicy Andhra Prawn Masala)

ingredients.name: Poppy seeds, cloves, cinnamon & coriander paste

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle curry leaves and slit green chillies, and fry chopped onions until deep golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add cleaned prawns, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt; cook on medium heat until the moisture released by the prawns mostly evaporates.
Stir in the ground poppy seed and spice paste with a splash of water, roast until thick and oil separates, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Traditional coastal Andhra semi-dry prawn curry that pairs wonderfully with steamed rice and rasam.

Mix the tempering into the cooked dal, adjust water and salt, and simmer briefly.

name: Assamese Maasor Dimo Tenga (Assamese Tangy Tomato & Lemon Fish Egg Curry)

ingredients.name: Potato, boiled and lightly mashed (for body)
Fresh lemon juice (kaji nemu) or tenga
Turmeric, green chillies, coriander leaves & salt

steps.text: Mix fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small golden fritters in mustard oil.
Temper oil with fenugreek and mustard seeds, add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, salt, and lightly mashed boiled potato; cook until tomatoes break down into a tangy sauce.
Pour in warm water, add the fish egg boras and slit green chillies, simmer 5 minutes, and finish off-heat with lemon juice and fresh coriander.

notes: Light, oil-sparing Assamese sour curry ideal for warm days.

name: Assamese Maasor Konir Bora (Assamese Herb & Onion Fish Egg Fritters)

Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan and fry flat spoonfuls on medium-low heat until crisp and golden brown on both sides.

notes: Rice flour gives Assamese Maasor Konir Bora its signature light crunch.

name: Banarasi Dum Aloo (Stuffed Potatoes in Rich Tomato-Fennel-Cashew Gravy)

ingredients.name: Medium potatoes, peeled and hollowed out
Roasted fennel (saunf), cumin, Kashmiri chilli & garam masala

steps.text: Scoop the center of peeled potatoes, fry the shells golden, and stuff with a mixture of crumbled paneer, fried scooped potato bits, cashews, raisins, and spices.
Cook tomato puree, ginger paste, cashew paste, roasted fennel powder, and Kashmiri chilli in ghee until velvety and rich.
Halve the stuffed potatoes, nestle into the hot gravy, and garnish with cream, kasuri methi, and coriander.

notes: Festive Banarasi banquet potato dish.

name: Bandhakopi Bharta (Steamed Cabbage Mash)

steps.text: Boil or steam shredded cabbage until soft, then squeeze out excess water thoroughly.
Heat mustard oil, fry dry red chillies and garlic cloves, and toss the cabbage over high heat for 3 minutes until dry.
Grind or mash coarsely and fold in chopped onion, green chilli, fresh coriander, salt, and a drop of raw mustard oil.

notes: Drying the steamed cabbage over high heat gives a smoky flavour.

name: Bandhakopi Chingri Ghonto (Bengali Cabbage with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Bay leaf, cumin seeds, garam masala, sugar & salt

steps.text: Toss prawns with salt and turmeric, fry lightly in mustard oil, and set aside. Fry cubed potatoes until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, cook ginger paste, tomato, and spices, then add shredded cabbage, potatoes, and salt. Cover and cook until soft.
Mix in green peas and fried prawns, cook uncovered until excess moisture dries up, and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: A beloved Bengali winter dish combining sweet winter cabbage and peas with savory small prawns.

ingredients.name: Crushed fennel (saunf), coriander seeds, cumin, hing & red chilli
Oil or ghee for frying & salt

steps.section: Knead or stuff spiced urad dough
steps.text: Sauté coarsely ground urad dal with hing, ginger-green chilli, crushed fennel, coriander, and spices; either knead directly into the wheat-semolina dough or stuff inside dough balls.
Roll slightly thicker than regular pooris and fry in medium-hot oil until crisp, flaky, and golden brown.

notes: Classic Old Delhi and Mathura street breakfast served with spicy hing-wale aloo sabzi.

name: Beetroot Bharta (Chukandar Mash)

steps.text: Peel beetroot, grate or cube, and steam/boil until tender.
Mash or mix the cooked beetroot with finely chopped onion, green chillies, roasted cumin, lemon juice, coriander, salt, and mustard oil.
Serve warm or at room temperature alongside rice, dal, or roti.

notes: Earthy beetroot pairs well with sharp mustard oil and lemon.

ingredients.name: Boiled or roasted beetroot, pureed smooth
Roasted cumin powder, ajwain, fennel powder & red chilli powder

steps.text: Combine wheat flour, semolina, spices, salt, 1 tbsp oil, and smooth beetroot puree to knead a firm dough.

steps.section: Roll and puff in hot oil
steps.text: Roll into small rounds and deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and crisp around the edges.

notes: Naturally colorful, nutrient-rich pooris that pair wonderfully with aloo rasedar or raita.

name: Begun Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Jhal (Eggplant, Potato & Fish Egg Mustard Medley)

steps.text: Fry eggplant wedges in mustard oil until golden and set aside. Pan-fry seasoned fish roe and cut into chunks.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, sauté sliced onion, potato wedges, and chopped tomato with turmeric and salt until potatoes are tender.

steps.section: Simmer with mustard, roe and eggplant
steps.text: Add mustard paste mixed with warm water, fried eggplant, and fish roe chunks; simmer for 5 minutes and garnish with coriander.

notes: Silky eggplant and fish roe soaked in a tangy mustard-tomato sauce.

name: Begun Bharta (Roasted Eggplant Mash)

steps.text: Wash the brinjal, make 2–3 slits to check for blemishes, optionally tuck garlic cloves and a green chilli inside, and rub the skin lightly with oil.
Roast directly over an open gas flame, turning frequently until the skin is completely charred and the flesh collapses softly.
Cool slightly, peel off the charred skin, and mash the smoky flesh with raw chopped onion, green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and pungent mustard oil.

notes: In Bengal this raw-onion mustard-oil mash is called Begun Pora / Begun Bharta and pairs wonderfully with hot roti or winter khichuri.

name: Begun Chingri Jhal (Eggplant & Prawn Mustard Curry)

steps.text: Season eggplant wedges and prawns with salt and turmeric. Fry eggplant until golden and lightly sear prawns; set both aside.
Temper mustard oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, sauté chopped tomato with turmeric, then add mustard paste strained with warm water.
Add fried eggplant and prawns to the bubbling gravy, simmer gently for 5 minutes, and drizzle raw mustard oil before serving.

notes: Silky fried eggplant absorbs the pungent mustard and prawn broth beautifully.

name: Bhandare Wale Aloo Ki Sabzi (Temple-Style No-Onion No-Garlic Tomato Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes, finely chopped or grated
Cumin seeds, fennel seeds, crushed coriander seeds, cloves & black peppercorns
Asafoetida (hing), grated ginger & slit green chillies
Kashmiri red chilli, turmeric, amchur, black salt & kasuri methi

steps.section: Roast coarsely crushed whole spices in ghee
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle cumin, fennel, crushed coriander seeds, cloves, peppercorns, bay leaf, dry red chilli, and a generous pinch of hing, then sauté grated ginger and green chillies.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and black salt; cook until oil separates.
Add hand-crushed boiled potatoes and hot water; simmer for 10 minutes until thick and aromatic, finishing with amchur, crushed kasuri methi, and coriander.

notes: Iconic North Indian temple-feast (bhandara) sabzi served with crispy bedmi puri or plain poori.

name: Bhanga Aloor Torkari (Bengali Hand-Crushed Potato Curry for Kochuri & Luchi)

ingredients.name: Potatoes, boiled and hand-crushed (bhanga) into uneven chunks
Turmeric, cumin powder & Bengali bhaja masala (roasted cumin-red chilli)
Green chillies, coriander leaves, sugar & salt

steps.text: Boil potatoes until tender, peel (or leave skin partially on), and break them roughly by hand (bhanga) instead of cutting with a knife so craggy edges release starch.

steps.section: Temper with panch phoron and hing
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle bay leaf, dry red chillies, panch phoron, and hing, then sauté grated ginger, green chillies, chopped tomato, turmeric, and cumin powder.

steps.section: Simmer and finish with bhaja masala
steps.text: Toss in the hand-broken potatoes, pour in warm water, salt, and a pinch of sugar, and simmer for 8 minutes until thick and glossy. Finish with roasted bhaja masala and fresh coriander.

notes: Hand-crushing (bhanga) the boiled potatoes gives this sweet-shop style curry its signature velvety, starchy gravy.

name: Bhapa Chingri (Steamed Mustard & Coconut Prawns)

ingredients.name: Yellow & black mustard seeds (soaked and ground)
Turmeric powder, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Grind soaked mustard seeds, poppy seeds, grated coconut, 2 green chillies, and a pinch of salt with a splash of water into a smooth paste.
In a steel tiffin box with a tight lid, toss cleaned prawns with the ground paste, whisked yogurt, turmeric, salt, sugar, and 1.5 tbsp raw mustard oil. Top with slit green chillies.
Close the lid tightly and steam in a covered pan with water reaching halfway up the box for 15-18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes before opening.

notes: Traditional Bengali steamed delicacy; grind mustard with a pinch of salt and green chilli to prevent bitterness.

name: Bhatura (Fluffy Punjabi Leavened Fried Bread)

ingredients.name: Baking powder (1/2 tsp) & baking soda (1/4 tsp)
Oil (for dough and deep frying) & salt

steps.text: Soak sooji in yogurt for 10 minutes, then mix with maida, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, salt, and 1 tbsp oil. Knead with warm water into a soft, smooth dough and rest covered for 1 hour.
Grease the rolling surface with oil (avoid dry flour) and roll each ball into an oval or large circle.
Slide into hot oil, press gently with a slotted spoon so it balloons immediately, flip once until golden, and serve with chole.

notes: Soaking semolina in yogurt gives bhaturas a crisp exterior that stays puffed.

Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Chandrapuli

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Cheese Chilli Garlic Paratha

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves & green chillies, finely minced
Oregano, red chilli flakes & black pepper

steps.text: Toss grated cheese with minced garlic, green chillies, fresh coriander, oregano, chilli flakes, and black pepper.
Roll dough into a circle, pile the cheese mixture in the center, fold all four edges into a sealed square envelope, and roll gently.
Cook on a medium-low tawa with butter until the crust is crisp and the cheese inside is molten.

name: Chemmeen Manga Curry (Kerala Raw Mango & Coconut Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Raw green mango, peeled and sliced

steps.text: Grind grated coconut with turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, and 3 shallots into a smooth paste.
In a clay pot (manchatti) or pan, combine ground coconut paste, water, raw mango slices, ginger, green chillies, and salt. Bring to a boil, then add prawns and cook for 8 minutes.
Heat coconut oil, splutter mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, sliced shallots, and curry leaves until golden, and pour over the curry.

notes: Tangy raw mango and creamy ground coconut make this one of Kerala's most iconic seafood curries.

name: Chettinad Prawn Masala (Eral Chettinad Curry)

ingredients.name: Chettinad masala (roasted peppercorns, fennel, cumin, coriander, dry red chillies)

steps.text: Dry-roast black pepper, fennel, cumin, coriander seeds, cinnamon, cloves, and red chillies; grind with grated coconut into a fragrant masala.
Heat sesame oil, temper with fennel seeds and curry leaves, sauté shallots and ginger-garlic paste until golden, then cook tomatoes until pulpy.
Stir in the ground Chettinad masala, add prawns and a splash of water, and simmer for 6-7 minutes until prawns are tender and coated in spicy gravy.

notes: Freshly roasted black pepper and fennel give Chettinad prawn masala its signature warmth.

name: Chichinda Bharta (Snake Gourd Mash)

steps.text: Scrape the outer skin lightly, remove pithy seeds if mature, and slice thinly.

steps.section: Cook with garlic and kalo jeere
steps.text: Sauté in mustard oil with nigella seeds, garlic, and green chillies until soft and dry.
Grind or mash with chopped onion, salt, and a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Light, savoury gourd mash that goes well with hot rice.

name: Chilli Prawns (Indo-Chinese Dry / Semi-Gravy)

ingredients.name: Soy sauce, red chilli sauce & tomato ketchup
Oil, white vinegar, black pepper & salt

steps.text: Toss prawns with cornflour, flour, black pepper, salt, and a splash of soy sauce. Crisp-fry in hot oil for 2-3 minutes and drain.
In a hot wok with 1 tbsp oil, stir-fry chopped garlic, ginger, and green chillies for 30 seconds, then toss in cubed onions and capsicum for 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar, and a splash of cornflour slurry. Toss in the crispy prawns and spring onion greens on high flame.

notes: Kolkata Tangra-style Indo-Chinese favorite; add 1/2 cup stock and extra cornflour slurry if you prefer a gravy version.

name: Chingri Aloo Dum (Bengali Spiced Potato & Prawn Dum)

ingredients.name: Baby potatoes or halved potatoes, parboiled
Cumin, coriander, Kashmiri chilli & turmeric powder
Bay leaf, whole garam masala, bhaja masala & salt

steps.text: Prick parboiled potatoes and fry in mustard oil with turmeric and salt until golden. Lightly sear prawns for 1-2 minutes and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf and whole garam masala, brown the chopped onion, and cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes and warm water, cover and cook on low heat for 6 minutes, then fold in prawns, simmer 4 minutes, and finish with ghee and roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Rich Bengali aloor dum elevated with juicy prawns; pairs wonderfully with luchi or parotta.

name: Chingri Bharta (Bengali Smoky Mashed Prawn with Mustard Oil)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, fry dry red chillies until crisp and set aside. Pan-roast garlic cloves and turmeric-salted prawns until cooked and lightly charred.
Coarsely mash or pulse the cooked prawns, roasted garlic, and crushed dry red chillies on a shil-nora (grinding stone) or food processor.
Fold in finely chopped raw onion, green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and 1 tbsp pungent raw mustard oil.

notes: A fiery, intensely flavorful Bengali & Bangladeshi mash served with steaming hot plain rice.

name: Chingri Diye Borboti Aloo (Yardlong Beans, Potato & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric, fry briefly in mustard oil, and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and sliced onion, add potato strips and yardlong beans, and sauté with turmeric, cumin, and coriander powder.
Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, and a splash of warm water; cover and cook until tender.

notes: Homestyle Bengali weekday vegetable-and-prawn curry.

name: Chingri Diye Chichinda (Snake Gourd with Small Prawns)

ingredients.name: Snake gourd (chichinda), scraped and thinly sliced

steps.text: Lightly fry turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, green chillies, and sliced onion; add sliced snake gourd, turmeric, and salt, and cook covered until soft.
Stir in fried prawns, grated coconut, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered until excess moisture evaporates.

notes: Light, wholesome monsoon side dish for steamed rice.

name: Chingri Diye Dhundul (Sponge Gourd with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Sponge gourd (dhundul / nenua), peeled and sliced
Mustard seeds or poppy seed paste

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric, sear lightly in mustard oil, and remove.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, add sliced sponge gourd, turmeric, and salt, and cook in its own natural juices.
Stir in mustard or poppy seed paste and fried prawns; simmer for 5 minutes until creamy.

notes: Soft, naturally sweet sponge gourd pairs delicately with small river prawns.

name: Chingri Diye Kakrol Aloo (Spiny Gourd, Potato & Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Nigella seeds, green chillies, turmeric & salt

steps.text: Lightly sear seasoned prawns and remove. Fry spiny gourd and potato wedges in mustard oil until lightly browned.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, sauté onion-ginger paste, cumin powder, and turmeric with a splash of water.
Add fried vegetables, warm water, and salt; cook until tender, then stir in prawns and mustard paste for 4 minutes.

notes: Seasonal monsoon gourd curry popular across West Bengal.

name: Chingri Diye Kanchkola Aloo Jhol (Raw Banana, Potato & Prawn Light Curry)

ingredients.name: Raw green banana (kanchkola), peeled and cut into wedges
Cumin seeds, bay leaf & green chillies

steps.section: Soak raw banana and sear prawns
steps.text: Soak cut raw banana in turmeric water to prevent darkening, then drain. Lightly fry prawns and potato wedges in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, cumin powder, and turmeric, then add raw banana, potatoes, and warm water.
Once vegetables are tender, add seared prawns and slit green chillies, and simmer for 4-5 minutes.

notes: Wholesome, stomach-friendly Bengali light lunch jhol.

name: Chingri Diye Korola Aloo Chorchori (Bitter Gourd, Potato & Prawn Medley)

steps.text: Fry bitter gourd slices in mustard oil until crisp-golden to reduce bitterness; lightly sear prawns and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron, sauté sliced onion and potato wedges with turmeric and salt until nearly tender.
Add fried bitter gourd, prawns, mustard paste, and a splash of water; cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.

notes: Traditional first-course Bengali bitter dish (shukto/teto) for lunch.

name: Chingri Diye Mulo Ghonto (White Radish with Small Prawns)

ingredients.name: White radish (mulo), grated or finely julienned
Nigella seeds (kalo jeere), bay leaf & dry red chilli
Turmeric, green chillies, coriander leaves, sugar & salt

steps.text: Lightly squeeze or parboil grated radish with a pinch of salt and drain excess water. Sear seasoned prawns in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and nigella seeds, fry finely cubed potatoes, then add radish, ginger paste, turmeric, and cumin powder.
Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, a pinch of sugar, and chopped coriander; cook until dry and fragrant.

notes: Classic Bengali winter radish preparation enriched with small prawns.

name: Chingri Diye Note Shak Chorchori (Amaranth Greens with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Amaranth greens & tender stems (note shak), chopped
Turmeric, green chillies, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Toss small prawns with salt and turmeric, sear in mustard oil, and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, fry potato and brinjal cubes, then add chopped amaranth stems and leaves with salt and turmeric.
Stir in fried prawns, mustard paste, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook until moisture evaporates.

notes: Summer leafy green chorchori loved across Bengal.

name: Chingri Diye Olkopi Dalna (Kohlrabi, Potato & Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Bay leaf, whole cumin, garam masala, coriander & salt

steps.text: Parboil cubed kohlrabi for 4 minutes, drain, and fry with potato cubes in mustard oil. Sear seasoned prawns and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, tomato, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add kohlrabi, potatoes, and warm water; simmer until tender, then add prawns, garam masala, and ghee.

notes: Winter kohlrabi (olkopi) and prawn curry.

name: Chingri Diye Palong Shak Ghonto (Spinach & Vegetable Medley with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Turmeric, green chillies, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil and remove. Fry cubed potato, radish, and brinjal until golden.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, sauté ginger paste and cumin powder, then add fried vegetables and chopped spinach.
Fold in fried prawns, slit green chillies, salt, and a pinch of sugar; cook until thick and cohesive.

notes: Traditional Bengali winter spinach ghonto with prawns.

name: Chingri Diye Pepe Aloo Jhol (Raw Papaya, Potato & Prawn Light Curry)

ingredients.name: Raw green papaya (pepe), peeled and cubed
Bay leaf, cumin seeds & green chillies

steps.text: Lightly sear turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil and remove. Sauté cubed raw papaya and potato for 4 minutes.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, add ginger paste, turmeric, cumin powder, papaya, potatoes, and warm water; cook covered until soft.
Stir in seared prawns, slit green chillies, and a drop of ghee; simmer for 5 minutes.

notes: Light, nourishing, and easy-to-digest Bengali everyday prawn curry.

name: Chingri Jhal (Bengali Spicy Prawn Mustard-Tomato Gravy)

ingredients.name: Turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander leaves & salt

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric and sear lightly in hot mustard oil for 1-2 minutes; set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, cook grated tomato with turmeric and chilli powder, then add mustard paste mixed with warm water.
Add seared prawns, simmer for 4-5 minutes until the gravy coats the prawns, and finish with chopped coriander and raw mustard oil.

notes: Quick, fiery Bengali prawn jhal ready in under 25 minutes.

name: Chingri Kalia (Festive Bengali Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Whole garam masala, cumin, Kashmiri chilli, sugar & salt

steps.text: Season cleaned prawns with turmeric and salt, fry briefly in hot mustard oil until golden-pink, and remove.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. Fry grated onion until deep golden, then cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, yogurt, and spices until oil separates.
Add warm water to form a rich gravy, return the prawns, simmer gently for 5-6 minutes, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Serve with basanti pulao, vegetable pulao, or steamed basmati rice.

name: Chingri Khichuri (Bengali Roasted Moong Dal Khichuri with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Bay leaf, dry red chilli, cumin, turmeric, garam masala & salt

steps.text: Dry-roast moong dal until golden and aromatic, then wash with Gobindobhog rice. Separately, fry seasoned prawns with ginger and spices in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and cumin seeds. Sauté ginger, tomato, turmeric, and cumin powder, then add washed rice, roasted dal, and hot water; cook until soft.
Gently fold the spiced fried prawns, slit green chillies, garam masala, and a generous spoonful of ghee into the hot khichuri.

notes: Coastal Bengali monsoon specialty pairing fragrant Gobindobhog khichuri with spiced prawns.

name: Chingri Kosha (Bengali Slow-Cooked Spicy Prawn Masala)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli, cumin, coriander & turmeric powder
Whole garam masala, ghee, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Coat prawns with turmeric and salt, sear in smoking mustard oil for 1 minute per side, and set aside.

Temper oil with whole garam masala and a pinch of sugar for color. Caramelize sliced onions, then slow-roast ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and spice powders with splashes of warm water until dark and glossy.
Add the seared prawns and slit green chillies to the rich masala, cook for 4-5 minutes until well coated, and finish with ghee.

notes: Delicious with luchi, radhaballabhi, parotta, or pulao.

name: Chingri Macher Bora (Bengali Prawn & Coconut Fritters)

ingredients.name: Small prawns (kucho or medium chingri), cleaned
Turmeric powder, kalonji, coriander leaves & salt

steps.text: Coarsely chop or pulse the cleaned prawns so they retain a bite.
Combine minced prawns with grated coconut, chopped onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, turmeric, kalonji, salt, and besan into a firm mixture.
Shape into flat round patties (bora) and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until crisp and golden brown.

notes: Serve hot as a starter with dal-bhaat (lentils and steamed rice) or as an evening snack with tea.

name: Chingri Macher Chop (Bengali Spiced Prawn Croquettes)

steps.text: Sauté onion, ginger, garlic, and chopped prawns with turmeric until cooked. Mix in mashed potatoes, bhaja masala, garam masala, green chillies, and coriander; cool completely.
Shape mixture into oval croquettes, roll in dry flour, dip in beaten egg or cornflour slurry, and coat generously in breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until deep golden brown and crunchy. Serve with kasundi and onion-cucumber salad.

notes: A classic Kolkata telebhaja / cabin snack.

name: Chingri Macher Jhol (Light Homestyle Bengali Prawn Broth)

steps.text: Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil and set aside. Fry potato wedges for 3 minutes.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, cook ginger paste, cumin-coriander powder, and tomato, then add warm water and potatoes.
Once potatoes are tender, add prawns and fresh coriander leaves; simmer gently for 5 minutes.

notes: Comforting, low-spice everyday Bengali prawn jhol.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Moong Dal (Roasted Moong Dal with Prawn Heads)

ingredients.name: Cleaned jumbo prawn heads (golda chingri matha) or small prawns
Cumin seeds, bay leaf & dry red chilli
Turmeric, cumin powder, garam masala, sugar & salt

steps.text: Dry-roast sona moong dal until golden and aromatic, wash thoroughly, and boil with salt and turmeric until soft but intact.
Heat mustard oil, temper with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and cumin seeds. Fry chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and seasoned prawn heads, crushing them slightly to release flavor.

steps.section: Simmer dal and finish with ghee
steps.text: Pour the boiled moong dal into the pan, simmer together for 5 minutes with a pinch of sugar, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Zero-waste Bengali delicacy that turns golda chingri heads into a rich, aromatic dal.

steps.text: Clean prawns and lightly season with salt and turmeric.
Lightly fry prawns, remove, then cook onion and ginger paste with spices.
Add coconut milk and a little water. Return prawns and simmer gently until just cooked.

name: Chingri Paturi (Banana Leaf Wrapped Mustard Prawns)

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds & poppy seeds (soaked and ground)
Banana leaves (cut into squares and wilted over flame)

steps.text: Grind mustard seeds, poppy seeds, grated coconut, and 2 green chillies into a thick, smooth paste. Mix with turmeric, salt, raw mustard oil, and cleaned prawns.
Spoon marinated prawns onto oiled, flame-softened banana leaf squares, top each parcel with a slit green chilli, and fold and tie securely with cotton thread.
Cook the banana leaf parcels in a lightly oiled covered skillet on low heat for 7-8 minutes per side until the leaves char and the aroma blooms.

notes: Wilting the banana leaves briefly over an open flame makes them pliable so they fold without tearing.

name: Chingri Posto (Prawns in Bengali Poppy Seed Paste)

ingredients.name: White poppy seeds (posto), soaked and ground smooth

steps.text: Soak white poppy seeds in warm water for 20 minutes, then grind with 2 green chillies and a splash of water into a creamy paste.
Lightly sear turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil for 1 minute. Temper the oil with nigella seeds and optional sliced onion until translucent.
Stir in the poppy seed paste, warm water, salt, and prawns. Simmer on low heat for 5 minutes and finish with raw mustard oil and slit green chillies.

notes: Keep spices minimal so the nutty sweetness of posto and mustard oil shines through.

name: Chingri Pulao (Bengali Gobindobhog Prawn Pilaf)

ingredients.name: Whole garam masala, bay leaf, green chillies, sugar & salt

steps.text: Wash and drain rice. Lightly fry seasoned prawns and set aside; fry cashews and raisins in ghee.
Temper ghee with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. Cook onion-ginger paste, then gently roast the drained rice for 2 minutes.

steps.section: Simmer with coconut milk and prawns
steps.text: Add coconut milk, warm water, salt, and a touch of sugar. When rice is 80% done, fold in the prawns, fried cashews, raisins, and green chillies; cover on low heat until fluffy.

notes: Fragrant Bengali one-pot prawn pilaf cooked with coconut milk and Gobindobhog rice.

name: Chini Porota (Bengali Sweet Sugar-Stuffed Layered Paratha)

ingredients.name: Warm water or milk & pinch of salt

steps.text: Knead flour with 1 tsp ghee, a pinch of salt, and warm water or milk into a soft dough.
Roll into a circle, brush with ghee, sprinkle evenly with sugar and cardamom powder, fold into a triangle or square parcel sealing the edges well, and roll out gently.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa with ghee until the sugar inside melts into a caramelized syrup and the outside turns golden and crisp.

notes: Nostalgic childhood favorite across Bengali and Indian households.

name: Daab Chingri (Prawns Cooked in Tender Coconut)

ingredients.name: Tender green coconut (daab) with water and soft malai
Turmeric powder, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Scoop 3 tbsp of soft tender coconut flesh (malai) and blend with mustard paste, posto-cashew paste, green chillies, and a splash of tender coconut water.
Lightly sear turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil for 1 minute, mix with the coconut-mustard gravy and coconut milk, and spoon inside the hollowed green coconut shell.
Cap the coconut with its top, seal the rim with flour dough, and bake at 180°C or steam in a deep covered pot for 30 minutes. Serve straight from the shell.

notes: One of Bengal's crown-jewel prawn delicacies; can also be steamed in a heatproof bowl with tender coconut water and malai.

name: Dahi Wale Aloo (Potatoes in Tangy Spiced Yogurt Gravy)

ingredients.name: Plain yogurt (curd), whisked with 1 tsp besan
Cumin seeds, mustard seeds, hing & curry leaves
Turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli & coriander powder

steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin seeds, mustard seeds, hing, curry leaves, chopped ginger, and green chillies.
Lower heat, pour in yogurt whisked with besan, turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder, and stir continuously until it comes to a gentle boil.
Add boiled potatoes and salt, simmer for 6 minutes until the tangy gravy thickens, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Quick 20-minute comfort curry when you have no tomatoes or onions on hand.

name: Dal Puri (Spiced Chana Dal Stuffed Fried Puri)

ingredients.name: Chana dal (split Bengal gram), soaked and boiled
Cumin seeds, dry red chillies & garlic/ginger
Mustard oil or ghee & oil for frying

steps.text: Boil soaked chana dal with turmeric and salt until tender but dry; mash or grind coarsely and sauté with cumin, dry red chilli, hing, ginger, and garam masala.
Stuff the spiced dal filling inside soft wheat-maida dough balls, seal carefully, and roll into medium discs.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown and puffed on both sides. Serve with kheer, pickle, or potato curry.

notes: Popular across Bengal, Bihar, and eastern UP for festive meals and monsoon days.

name: Dalgona Coffee

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Data Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Chorchori (Drumstick, Potato & Fish Egg Chorchori)

ingredients.name: Drumsticks (sajne data), peeled and cut into batons

steps.text: Sear seasoned fish roe in mustard oil until firm, break into bite-sized pieces, and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, sauté sliced onion, potato strips, drumstick batons, tomato, turmeric, and salt with a splash of water covered until tender.

steps.section: Finish with mustard paste and roe
steps.text: Stir in mustard paste, slit green chillies, and fried fish roe pieces; cook for 5 minutes until coated.

notes: Seasonal spring-summer Bengali chorchori.

name: Dhakai Porota (Bengali Multi-Layered Flaky Fried Paratha)

ingredients.name: Ghee & cornflour/rice flour (for sata layering paste)

steps.section: Knead dough and whip sata paste
steps.text: Knead maida with 2 tbsp ghee, sugar, salt, and warm milk-water into a smooth dough. Whisk melted ghee and cornflour into a creamy layering paste (sata).
Roll a dough ball into a large circle, spread sata paste, make a radial cut from center to edge, and roll tightly into a cone. Press the cone flat from the tip down and roll gently into a disc.
Shallow-deep fry in hot oil and ghee over medium heat, continuouslyspooning hot oil into the center so dozens of crisp, flaky rings open up.

notes: Traditional Dhaka-style layered flaky porota served with kosha mangsho or cholar dal.

ingredients.name: Cumin, coriander, turmeric & Kashmiri chilli powder
Whole garam masala, bay leaf, garam masala powder & salt

steps.text: Boil cubed raw jackfruit with salt and turmeric until just tender, then drain and lightly fry along with potato cubes. Lightly fry prawns and set aside.
Temper mustard oil with bay leaf and whole garam masala. Fry onions until golden, then slow-cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and ground spices until oil separates.
Add jackfruit and potatoes, coat well in the masala, pour warm water, and simmer until tender. Add fried prawns for the last 5 minutes and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: A beloved Bengali summer banquet dish where raw jackfruit absorbs the rich prawn and spice gravy.

Shred and mash the cooked jackfruit while warm.

notes: Known as Echorer Bharta in Bengal and Kathal ka Chokha in Bihar.

name: Fish Egg Bhurji (Macher Dimer Jhuri Bhaja / Spiced Scrambled Fish Roe)

ingredients.name: Fish eggs / fish roe, cleaned and membrane removed
Turmeric, cumin, red chilli & garam masala powder
Fresh coriander leaves, lemon juice & salt

steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry finely chopped onions, minced garlic, ginger, and green chillies until golden.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, cumin, red chilli powder, and salt, then tip in the mashed fish eggs and stir-fry continuously on medium-low heat.
Keep stirring until the roe separates into golden, savory granules (jhuri). Finish with garam masala, lemon juice, and fresh coriander.

notes: Delicious scrambled fish roe bhurji that can be eaten with hot rice, roti, or buttered toast.

name: Fish Egg Curry (Homestyle Indian Macher Dimer Curry)

ingredients.name: Fish eggs / fish roe sacs, cleaned
Turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli, cumin & coriander powder
Whole spices, garam masala, coriander leaves & salt

steps.text: Simmer the fish roe sacs gently in salted turmeric water for 5-6 minutes until firm, cool slightly, cut into bite-sized cubes, and lightly sear in oil.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf, brown the chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste, then cook tomatoes and spice powders until oil separates.
Add warm water to form a smooth gravy, add the seared fish egg cubes, simmer gently for 6 minutes, and finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.

notes: Poaching and cubing the roe allows it to hold its shape like paneer cubes in the curry.

name: Fish Egg Fritter Curry (Macher Dimer Borar Jhol)

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into lengthwise wedges
Onion, finely chopped (half for boras, half for gravy)
Bay leaf, cumin seeds, green chillies, turmeric, garam masala & salt

steps.section: Make and fry fish egg boras
steps.text: Mix fish eggs with half the chopped onion, chopped green chilli, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small boras in mustard oil until golden and set aside.
In the remaining oil, temper with bay leaf and cumin seeds, fry potato wedges and remaining onion, then cook ginger paste, tomato, turmeric, cumin, and coriander powder.
Pour in warm water, cover and cook until potatoes are tender, then drop in the fried fish egg boras and simmer for 4-5 minutes so they soak up the gravy. Finish with garam masala.

notes: Quintessential Bengali homestyle fish egg fritter curry served with steamed rice.

name: Fish Egg Fritters (Macher Dimer Bora)

ingredients.name: Fish eggs / fish roe (Rohu or Katla macher dim), washed and membrane removed

steps.text: Wash the fish roe gently, peel off the thin outer membrane, and mash the eggs in a bowl so no tough lumps remain.
Add finely chopped onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, nigella seeds, turmeric, salt, besan, and rice flour; whisk vigorously for 2 minutes to aerate.
Heat mustard oil in a pan over medium-low flame, drop spoonfuls of the mixture, and fry slowly on both sides until crisp outside and cooked through inside.

notes: Fry on medium-low heat and cover briefly if needed, as fish eggs pop slightly in hot oil.

name: Fish Egg Masala (Macher Dimer Kosha / Spicy Fish Roe Masala)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chilli, cumin, coriander & turmeric powder
Whole garam masala, garam masala powder, coriander & salt

steps.text: Steam or poach the fish roe with salt and turmeric until firm, cut into thick squares, and sear in hot mustard oil until golden.
Temper oil with whole garam masala, caramelize sliced onions, and slow-roast ginger-garlic paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders with splashes of water until dark and glossy.
Add the fried fish roe pieces and a splash of warm water, cook for 5 minutes until coated in thick masala, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Rich, spicy fish egg masala that pairs great with steamed rice, roti, or paratha.

name: Fish Egg Pakora (Crispy Macher Dimer Pakora)

ingredients.name: Carom seeds (ajwain), turmeric & red chilli powder
Mustard oil or vegetable oil for deep frying

steps.text: Combine cleaned fish eggs with sliced onion, ginger-garlic paste, chopped green chillies, coriander, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, lemon juice, salt, besan, and cornflour.
Drop small bite-sized portions into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden brown and crunchy.
Drain on paper towels, dust with chaat masala, and serve hot with kasundi or mint-coriander chutney.

notes: Crunchy evening snack that pairs wonderfully with masala chai or as a starter with dal-rice.

name: Fish Egg Potato Curry (Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Jhol)

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
Cumin, coriander, turmeric & red chilli powder
Cumin seeds, bay leaf, garam masala, coriander & salt

steps.text: Season fish roe with salt and turmeric, sear whole or in thick slabs in mustard oil until firm, and cut into pieces. Fry potato wedges in the same oil.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf, fry chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook tomato and spice powders.
Add potatoes and warm water; cook until tender, then add the fish roe pieces, simmer 5 minutes, and garnish with garam masala and coriander.

notes: Classic homestyle fish egg and potato curry.

ingredients.name: Baking powder (1/2 tsp) & baking soda (1/4 tsp)

steps.text: Knead maida, yogurt, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, salt, and warm water into a soft dough; rest covered for 30-45 minutes.
Roll into teardrop shapes, press minced garlic, kalonji, and chopped coriander on top, and brush the underside with water.
Stick the wet side onto a hot iron tawa (not non-stick). Once bubbles rise, invert the tawa directly over the gas flame until charred spots appear, then brush with melted garlic butter.

notes: Sticking the water-brushed underside to a hot iron tawa replicates tandoor char at home.

steps.text: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve 1/2 cup starchy pasta cooking water before draining.
Heat olive oil and butter in a wide pan, gently toast sliced garlic and chilli flakes, and sear seasoned prawns for 2 minutes per side until pink.
Add drained pasta, reserved pasta water, lemon juice, and parsley; toss vigorously over medium heat until coated in a glossy garlic-butter glaze.

notes: Quick 25-minute weeknight dinner; top with grated Parmesan or extra herbs if desired.

steps.text: Mash softened butter with finely minced garlic, chopped coriander, and chilli flakes.
Roll dough thin, spread with garlic butter, dust with dry flour, pleat like a paper fan, coil into a spiral, and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa until golden and crisp, then gently scrunch to separate the garlicky flaky layers.

notes: Restaurant-style garlic lachha paratha great with paneer, chicken, or prawn curries.

ingredients.name: White pepper, pinch of sugar & salt

Sauté minced garlic and spring onion whites until golden and aromatic. Stir in chilli paste, ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, and 1/2 cup water.
Thicken with cornflour slurry, return the prawns to the wok, and garnish with spring onion greens.

notes: Pairs wonderfully with vegetable or egg fried rice and hakka noodles.

steps.text: Grind grated coconut, Kashmiri red chillies, coriander seeds, turmeric, garlic, and tamarind with water into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil, sauté chopped onion and green chillies until soft, add the ground coconut paste and water, and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the cleaned fish roe pieces and kokum petals, season with salt, and simmer gently for 7 minutes until the roe is cooked through.

notes: Authentic Goan Gabhache Hooman served with steamed parboiled rice.

name: Goan Prawn Curry (Ambotik / Coconut Kokum Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Kokum petals or raw mango slices
Coconut oil, slit green chillies & salt

steps.text: Grind grated coconut, Kashmiri red chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, turmeric, garlic, and tamarind with warm water into a silky orange-red paste.
Heat coconut oil, fry chopped onion and slit green chillies until translucent, then pour in the ground masala paste and water; simmer for 6 minutes.
Add cleaned prawns, kokum petals, and salt; simmer gently for 5-6 minutes until the prawns curl and are cooked through.

notes: Authentic coastal Goan curry best enjoyed with steamed red or parboiled rice.

name: Gobi Bharta (Roasted Cauliflower / Phulkopi Mash)

steps.text: Wash cauliflower florets in warm salted water, steam or parboil until tender, and lightly char in a pan.
Heat mustard oil, sauté onion, ginger, garlic, and green chilli until golden, then cook chopped tomato and turmeric until soft.
Mash the cauliflower into the pan, season with salt, cook together for 3–4 minutes, and finish with fresh coriander.

notes: For a Bengali Phulkopi Bharta variation, skip the tomato and mash boiled florets directly with raw mustard oil, roasted red chilli, onion, and coriander.

name: Golda Chingri Malaikari (Jumbo River Prawn Coconut Milk Curry)

ingredients.name: Jumbo freshwater prawns (Golda Chingri), shells trimmed with head/tail intact
Bay leaf, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, sugar & salt

steps.text: Devein jumbo golda prawns while keeping the head and tail shell intact for flavor. Rub with salt and turmeric, sear lightly in mustard oil for 2 minutes, and remove.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Cook onion and ginger paste with turmeric and Kashmiri chilli powder until oil separates.
Pour in coconut milk and a splash of warm water, add prawns, slit green chillies, salt, and a pinch of sugar. Simmer covered for 8 minutes and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: Keeping the head and tail shell intact infuses the coconut milk gravy with deep scampi flavor.

name: Golden Fried Prawns (Crispy Batter-Fried Prawns)

ingredients.name: Large prawns (peeled, deveined, tails on and butterflied)

steps.text: Make a shallow slit along the back of each prawn to butterfly it flat, pat dry, and season with salt, white pepper, and ginger-garlic juice.
Whisk flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt, 1 tsp oil, and ice-cold water into a smooth batter.
Hold each prawn by the tail, dip into the batter, and deep-fry in medium-hot oil for 3 minutes until puffed, golden, and crisp.

notes: Serve hot with sweet chilli dipping sauce or hot garlic sauce.

ingredients.name: Oil, mustard seeds, fenugreek, garlic cloves & curry leaves

steps.text: Sauté gongura leaves with 2 green chillies and a little oil until wilted and soft, then mash into a coarse tangy paste.
Heat oil, temper with mustard, fenugreek, crushed garlic, dry red chillies, and curry leaves. Fry chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste, then cook prawns with spice powders.
Stir in the mashed gongura paste and a splash of water; simmer for 6 minutes until oil floats to the top.

notes: Signature Andhra delicacy pairing the natural tang of sorrel leaves with sweet, juicy prawns.

ingredients.name: Panch phoron or cumin-fennel seeds & dry red chilli
Turmeric, coriander, red chilli & amchur / bhaja masala

steps.section: Bloom hing and spices in oil
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle dry red chilli and panch phoron/cumin, and add hing and ginger-green chilli paste so the aroma blooms.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, coriander, and red chilli powder; cook until soft and pulpy.
Add boiled cubed/crushed potatoes and warm water; simmer for 8-10 minutes until thick. Finish with bhaja masala, coriander leaves, and a topping of crispy sev.

notes: Famous Bura Bazar / Kolkata morning breakfast potato curry served with Hinger Kochuri or Club Kachori.

name: Hinger Kochuri (Kolkata Club Kachori Style Asafoetida Puri)

ingredients.name: Urad dal (biuli dal), soaked and ground, or sattu
Ginger-green chilli paste & roasted fennel-cumin powder

steps.text: Sauté ground urad dal (or sattu) in oil with a generous dose of hing, ginger-green chilli paste, roasted fennel-cumin powder, salt, and a pinch of sugar until dry.
Knead maida and sooji with melted ghee, salt, and water. Stuff small dough balls with the hing mixture and roll into crisp puris.
Fry in medium-hot oil until golden and crisp. Serve with spicy street-style potato curry (aloor torkari).

notes: Famous North Kolkata sweet-shop morning breakfast kochuri.

name: Ilish Macher Dimer Bora (Hilsa Fish Egg Fritters)

ingredients.name: Hilsa fish eggs (Ilish macher dim), intact lobes or mashed

steps.text: Wash the Hilsa roe lobes very gently without breaking the sac, pat dry, and rub evenly with salt, turmeric, and a pinch of red chilli powder.
Heat mustard oil in a skillet until lightly smoking, lower the flame, and fry the Hilsa roe with slit green chillies for 4-5 minutes per side covered until golden and firm.

steps.section: Slice and serve with fragrant oil
steps.text: Cut into thick slices and serve immediately over steaming hot plain rice drizzled with the aromatic Hilsa-infused frying oil.

notes: Keep spices minimal for Hilsa roe so its prized, buttery monsoon flavor takes center stage.

name: Ilish Macher Dimer Jhal (Hilsa Fish Roe Mustard-Tomato Gravy)

steps.text: Rub Hilsa roe lobes gently with salt and turmeric and sear lightly in hot mustard oil for 2 minutes per side.
Temper the Hilsa-scented oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, sauté grated tomato and turmeric, and stir in mustard paste with warm water.
Return the Hilsa roe lobes to the pan, simmer covered for 5-6 minutes, and finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Delicate monsoon Hilsa roe curry best enjoyed with plain steamed rice.

name: Ilish Macher Dimer Tok (Hilsa Roe in Tangy Tamarind Gravy)

steps.text: Season Hilsa roe with salt and turmeric, shallow-fry in mustard oil for 3 minutes per side, and slice into thick pieces.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, pour in tamarind water, turmeric, salt, mustard paste, and jaggery, and boil for 4 minutes.
Add the fried Hilsa roe slices and simmer gently for 4 minutes.

notes: Traditional East Bengali (Bangal) heirloom recipe pairing rich Hilsa roe with tangy tamarind.

ingredients.name: Crushed coriander seeds & dry mango powder (amchur)
Green chillies & grated ginger, finely chopped
Asafoetida (hing), turmeric, red chilli flakes & kasuri methi

steps.text: Heat ghee or oil in a wide pan, add cumin seeds, crushed coriander seeds, hing, ginger, and green chillies; let them sizzle without burning.
Add boiled potato cubes, turmeric, red chilli flakes, amchur, and salt; toss on medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes until golden and crusted with cumin.
Sprinkle crushed kasuri methi and fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

notes: Chill boiled potatoes for 30 minutes before cubing so they hold their shape and crisp up nicely.

Heat ghee or oil, add spices and vegetables if using, and stir until fragrant.
Add rice and measured water, cover and cook until tender. Rest briefly before serving.

name: Jhinge Aloo Chingri (Ridge Gourd, Potato & Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Ridge gourd (jhinge), peeled and cut into wedges

steps.text: Lightly fry turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil and remove. Fry potato wedges until golden.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, add ridge gourd, cumin-ginger paste, and turmeric; sauté for 4 minutes.
Add warm water and salt, cook covered until potatoes and ridge gourd are soft, then add prawns and simmer for 4 minutes.

notes: A soothing, light Bengali summer lunch curry (jhol) that is easy to digest.

name: Jhinge Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Borar Jhol (Ridge Gourd, Potato & Fish Egg Fritter Curry)

ingredients.name: Ridge gourd (jhinge), peeled and cut into wedges
Nigella seeds (kalo jeere), green chillies, turmeric & salt

steps.text: Mix fish eggs with chopped onion, green chilli, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small fritters in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, fry potato wedges, then add ridge gourd, ginger-cumin paste, turmeric, and warm water.
Once vegetables are soft, add the fried fish egg boras and simmer gently for 4-5 minutes.

notes: Light, cooling Bengali summer jhol.

name: Jhinge Bharta (Ridge Gourd / Turai Mash)

steps.text: Scrape the sharp ridges, peel lightly, and chop the ridge gourd (and clean peels if tender) into pieces.
Heat mustard oil, add kalo jeere, garlic, and green chillies, then add the ridge gourd and cook until tender and dry.
Grind or mash the cooked mixture with chopped onion, salt, and a few drops of raw mustard oil.

notes: Both the flesh and the tender ridged peel of jhinge make a delicious bharta.

name: Jhuri Aloo Bhaja (Bengali Crispy Matchstick Fried Potatoes with Peanuts)

ingredients.name: Black salt, regular salt & optional turmeric

steps.text: Rinse finely julienned potatoes in cold water 3-4 times until the water runs completely clear to remove starch, then spread on a kitchen towel until bone-dry.
Fry raw peanuts, dry red chillies, and curry leaves in hot oil until crisp; drain and set aside.
Fry the dry potato matchsticks in batches in hot oil until golden and crunchy. Drain on paper towels and toss with fried peanuts, curry leaves, and black salt.

notes: Do not salt the potatoes before frying so they turn out ultra-crispy.

ingredients.name: Raw green mango (kacha aam), peeled and cut into wedges
Mustard seeds & dry red chilli (for tempering)

steps.text: Beat fish roe with besan, salt, and turmeric; fry small golden fritters in mustard oil.

steps.section: Cook raw mango in mustard broth
steps.text: Temper oil with mustard seeds and dry red chilli, sauté green mango wedges with turmeric and salt, then add water and cook until mango softens.

steps.section: Simmer with mustard paste and boras
steps.text: Stir in mustard paste, sugar, and fried fish egg boras; simmer for 4 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature.

ingredients.name: Green chillies & roasted dry red chilli

steps.text: Wash raw green bananas, cut in halves with skin on, and boil or pressure-cook until fork-tender.
Peel the warm bananas (reserve the skins for Kanchkola Khosa Bharta if desired) and mash immediately while hot so no lumps form.
Mix in chopped onion, grated ginger, crushed chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and mustard oil or ghee.

notes: Always mash raw bananas while still hot, as they firm up quickly on cooling.

name: Kacha Tomato Bharta (Green Tomato Mash)

steps.text: Halve green tomatoes and pan-roast with garlic cloves and green chillies in a few drops of mustard oil until blistered and soft.
Mash the roasted green tomatoes, garlic, and chillies into a tangy coarse paste.
Fold in chopped onion, optional mustard paste, fresh coriander, salt, and raw mustard oil.

notes: Tangy and vibrant winter relish.

name: Kadai Prawns (Prawns with Bell Peppers & Kadai Masala)

ingredients.name: Kadai masala (roasted coriander seeds, dry red chillies, cumin)

steps.section: Pound kadai spice and toss peppers
steps.text: Dry-roast coriander seeds, cumin, and whole red chillies; crush coarsely. Quickly toss cubed onion petals and bell peppers in hot oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Sauté finely chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste until golden, add tomatoes and crushed kadai masala, and cook until oil separates.
Add prawns, sautéed bell peppers, and onion petals; cook for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender. Finish with crushed kasuri methi and ginger juliennes.

notes: Serve hot with garlic naan, tandoori roti, or jeera rice.

Boil or steam kakrol slices with a pinch of salt and turmeric until tender, drain well, and sear in mustard oil with nigella seeds, garlic, and green chillies.
Mash or grind the cooked kakrol mixture into a smooth bharta, fold in finely chopped onion and a drizzle of raw mustard oil, and serve warm.

notes: Remove hard seeds if the kakrol is over-ripe before mashing.

steps.text: Boil clean raw banana peels in water with a pinch of turmeric and salt until completely tender, then drain.
Grind the boiled peels with garlic cloves and green chillies into a smooth paste.
Heat mustard oil, crackle nigella seeds, add the ground paste and salt, and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until dark, glossy, and aromatic.

notes: Rich in iron and fibre; a staple Bengali comfort dish.

name: Karela Bharta (Bitter Gourd Mash)

ingredients.name: Green chilli or roasted red chilli

steps.text: Wash and slice karela thinly, rub with 1/2 tsp salt and turmeric, rest for 10 minutes, and squeeze out excess bitter juice.
Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry or steam-fry the karela slices with garlic on medium-low heat until tender and lightly browned.
Coarsely mash or pound the cooked karela with finely chopped onion, crushed chilli, salt, and a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Salting and resting karela before cooking mellows the bitterness while keeping its digestive benefits.

name: Kasha Aloor Dum (Bengali Spicy Slow-Braised Onion-Garlic Potato Dum)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli, cumin, coriander & turmeric powder
Whole garam masala, bay leaf, sugar & salt

steps.text: Parboil halved potatoes with salt and turmeric for 5 minutes, drain, and fry in hot mustard oil until golden-crusted.
Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, and a pinch of sugar. Caramelize onions, then slow-braise ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spices with splashes of warm water until dark and glossy.
Add the fried potatoes and a cup of warm water, cover and cook on low flame until the thick masala coats the potatoes, and finish with ghee.

notes: Rich, meaty-style Bengali kosha gravy for potatoes.

name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo (Fennel & Yogurt Spiced Baby Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Baby potatoes, peeled and pricked all over
Kashmiri red chilli powder (dissolved in water)

steps.text: Prick parboiled baby potatoes thoroughly with a fork or toothpick and fry in hot mustard oil until a golden-brown skin forms all around.
Whisk yogurt with Kashmiri red chilli paste, fennel powder (saunf), and dry ginger powder (sonth). Temper 2 tbsp oil with cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon, and hing.
Stir the spiced yogurt into the pan on low flame until boiling, add the fried baby potatoes and salt, and simmer covered on low heat for 10 minutes so the potatoes soak up the gravy.

notes: Authentic Kashmiri Pandit recipe made without onion, garlic, or tomatoes.

name: Kashmiri Kahwa

Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Keema Paratha (Spiced Minced Meat Stuffed Paratha)

ingredients.name: Onion, ginger, garlic & green chillies, finely chopped
Cumin, coriander, turmeric, red chilli & garam masala powder

steps.text: Sauté chopped onion, ginger-garlic, and green chillies in 1 tbsp oil, add minced meat and spice powders, and cook until completely dry. Stir in mint and coriander and cool completely.
Fill soft dough balls with the cooled dry keema mixture, seal tightly, and roll into parathas.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and golden brown on both sides. Serve with mint raita.

notes: Make sure the cooked keema has zero moisture and is completely cool before stuffing.

name: Kerala Chemmeen Roast (Nadan Spicy Prawn Fry)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli, black pepper, fennel & turmeric powder

steps.text: Cook cleaned prawns with turmeric, half the chilli powder, salt, curry leaves, and soaked kudampuli in a little water for 4 minutes.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pan, add extra curry leaves, crushed ginger-garlic, and sliced shallots; sauté until deep golden brown.
Add chopped tomato, remaining chilli, fennel, and black pepper powder, then tip in the prawns and roast on medium-low heat until dark and richly coated.

notes: Coconut oil, shallots, and fresh curry leaves give this Kerala toddy-shop classic its signature aroma.

name: Kerala Fish Roe Roast (Meen Mutta Roast with Shallots & Curry Leaves)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chilli, crushed black pepper, fennel & turmeric powder

steps.text: Heat coconut oil in a heavy pan, splutter curry leaves, and sauté crushed ginger-garlic and sliced shallots until golden brown.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, fennel, and black pepper powder; cook until thick and oil separates.
Add the fish roe (whole slices or coarse chunks), cover on low heat for 5 minutes until cooked, then stir-roast with extra curry leaves and lemon juice.

notes: Spicy, aromatic Kerala toddy-shop style Meen Mutta Roast.

name: Kerala Prawn Moilee (Chemmeen Molee in Coconut Milk)

ingredients.name: Ginger & garlic juliennes, slit green chillies
Mustard seeds, whole spices, turmeric, black pepper & salt

steps.text: Toss prawns with turmeric, black pepper, lemon juice, and salt for 10 minutes.

steps.section: Sauté aromatics and simmer in thin milk
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, cloves, cinnamon, and curry leaves. Soften sliced onion, ginger, garlic, and green chillies without browning, add thin coconut milk and prawns, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add tomato slices and thick coconut milk, warm gently for 2 minutes without boiling rigorously, and remove from heat.

notes: Delicate, mildly spiced Syrian Christian Kerala stew best served with appam, idiyappam, or steamed rice.

name: Khasta Dal Kachori (Flaky Moong Dal Stuffed Puri)

ingredients.name: Yellow moong dal, soaked 2 hours and coarsely ground
Crushed fennel, coriander seeds, cumin, hing, ginger & amchur
Ghee (for moyan shortening) & oil for slow frying

steps.text: Sauté hing, crushed fennel, coriander, cumin, and besan in 1 tbsp oil, add coarse moong dal, red chilli, amchur, and salt, and roast until dry and crumbly.

steps.section: Knead flaky moyan dough and stuff
steps.text: Rub 4 tbsp melted ghee into maida until breadcrumb-like, knead with cold water, stuff with dal balls, and flatten gently with your palm.
Slide into warm (low-medium) oil and fry slowly for 10-12 minutes until puffed, golden, and shatteringly flaky (khasta).

notes: Frying on low heat is the secret to a crisp, blister-free khasta kachori.
