name: Khosa-Soho Aloor Torkari (Kolkata Kochuri-Shop Skin-On Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Potatoes, scrubbed clean and cubed with skin on
Black chickpeas (kala chana, soaked) or green peas (optional)
Panch phoron & whole dry red chillies

steps.text: Heat mustard oil until smoking, then temper with whole dry red chillies, panch phoron, and a generous pinch of hing.
Add scrubbed skin-on potato cubes, soaked kala chana, ginger-green chilli paste, turmeric, and salt; stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Add warm water, cover and cook until potatoes are soft, lightly mash a few pieces into the gravy, and finish with a pinch of sugar and roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Authentic Kolkata street-corner kochuri and petai porota accompaniment.

name: Kochu Shak Chingri (Colocasia Stems & Greens with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Colocasia stems and greens (kochu shak), peeled and chopped
Nigella seeds (kalo jeere), bay leaf & dry red chilli

steps.text: Boil chopped colocasia stems with salt until soft, then drain thoroughly and mash coarsely.
Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil. Temper the oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, nigella seeds, crushed garlic, and green chillies.
Add mashed kochu shak, turmeric, salt, sugar, grated coconut, and fried prawns. Cook on medium heat, stirring continuously, until all moisture evaporates. Finish with lemon juice.

notes: Adding a squeeze of lemon juice at the end balances the earthy taro greens.

name: Kochu Shak Diye Macher Dim (Colocasia Greens with Fish Eggs)

ingredients.name: Colocasia stems & greens (kochu shak), peeled and chopped
Nigella seeds (kalo jeere), bay leaf & dry red chilli

steps.section: Boil kochu shak and fry roe
steps.text: Boil chopped colocasia stems with salt until soft, drain thoroughly, and mash. Fry seasoned fish roe in mustard oil until golden and crumble coarsely.

steps.section: Temper with garlic and kalo jeere
steps.text: Temper mustard oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, nigella seeds, crushed garlic, and green chillies.
Add mashed kochu shak, turmeric, salt, sugar, and crumbled fried fish roe; stir-cook until moisture dries up completely and finish with lemon juice.

notes: Rich, garlicky taro greens elevated with savory fried fish roe granules.

name: Kochur Loti Chingri (Taro Stolons with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Taro stolons (kochur loti), peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces

steps.text: Briefly blanch cleaned taro stolons in salted turmeric water for 2 minutes and drain well.
Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, fry sliced onion, garlic paste, and seasoned prawns with turmeric and chilli powder.
Add blanched kochur loti, mustard paste, grated coconut, and slit green chillies. Cook covered on low heat until tender and lightly caramelized.

notes: A prized East Bengali (Bangal) delicacy celebrated for its bold garlic, mustard, and prawn flavors.

name: Kochur Mukhi Bharta (Taro Root / Arbi Mash)

ingredients.name: Kochur Mukhi / Gathi Kochu / Arbi (Taro root)

steps.text: Wash taro roots and boil or pressure-cook with skins on until soft, then cool slightly and slip off the skins.
Mash the peeled taro roots smoothly with chopped onion, crushed roasted garlic and chillies, lemon juice, salt, and mustard oil.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve warm with steamed rice and dal.

notes: Creamy texture that pairs wonderfully with plain masoor or moong dal.

name: Kokum Sharbat

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Kolmi no Patio (Parsi Sweet, Sour & Spicy Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Heat oil with curry leaves and fry finely chopped onions until deep golden brown.
Add garlic-cumin-chilli paste and turmeric, sauté for 2 minutes, then add tomatoes and cook down into a thick, jammy masala.

steps.section: Simmer prawns with jaggery and vinegar
steps.text: Add prawns, jaggery, vinegar, and salt; cook for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender and the sweet-sour-spicy balance comes together.

notes: Traditionally served alongside Parsi yellow dal (Dhan Dar) and steamed rice.

name: Koraishutir Kochuri (Bengali Green Peas Stuffed Puri)

ingredients.name: Ghee or oil (for moyan and frying)

steps.text: Blend green peas, ginger, and green chillies into a smooth paste. Heat 1 tbsp oil with hing, add the pea paste, roasted cumin-coriander powder, salt, and sugar, and stir-cook until it leaves the sides of the pan.
Knead maida with 2 tbsp ghee, salt, and warm water into a pliable dough. Fill each dough cup with a ball of cooled pea stuffing, seal, and roll gently.
Deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and lightly golden. Serve with notun aloor dum and nolen gurer payesh.

notes: The quintessential Bengali winter breakfast and feast delicacy.

steps.text: Wash tiny shrimps thoroughly in a colander, drain completely, and toss with salt and turmeric powder.
Heat mustard oil in a wide pan, add the shrimps, and fry over medium-high heat until moisture evaporates and they turn crisp.
Add sliced onions and green chillies, stir-fry until onions are golden-brown, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Crunchy, savory Bengali starter accompaniment for hot rice and masoor dal.

Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, and a splash of water. Cover and cook until pumpkin is soft and slightly mashed; garnish with coriander leaves.

Coarsely mash or pulse with chopped onion, salt, and coriander leaves.

notes: Pan-roasting kundru brings out a pleasant nutty flavour.

Nigella seeds (kalo jeere) & dry red chillies

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with dry red chillies and nigella seeds, and fry cubed potatoes with turmeric and salt until golden and tender.
Sprinkle whole white poppy seeds (posto) and slit green chillies over the potatoes and stir-fry on medium-high flame for 3-4 minutes until the posto toasts nutty and crunchy.

notes: Toasted poppy seeds form a crunchy, nutty crust around the fried potatoes.

name: Lau Bharta (Bottle Gourd Mash)

steps.text: Peel the bottle gourd, remove any large seeds, and grate or chop finely.
Simmer the bottle gourd covered in its own juices with a pinch of salt until soft, then uncover and cook until excess water evaporates.
Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, garlic, onion, and green chillies, add the cooked gourd, and mash on the pan until cohesive. Garnish with coriander.

notes: Light, cooling, and easy to digest.

ingredients.name: Tender bottle gourd (lau), peeled and finely cubed

steps.text: Season cleaned prawns with salt and turmeric, sear lightly in mustard oil for 2 minutes, and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and cumin seeds. Sauté ginger paste and cumin-coriander powder, then add finely cubed bottle gourd and salt. Cover and let it cook in its own juices.
Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar. Simmer until tender, then finish with chopped coriander leaves and a drop of ghee.

notes: One of the most iconic, comforting heirloom dishes of every Bengali household.

name: Lau Diye Macher Dimer Borar Jhol (Bottle Gourd & Fish Egg Fritter Curry)

ingredients.name: Bay leaf, cumin seeds, green chillies, coriander leaves, turmeric & salt

steps.text: Whisk fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, salt, and turmeric; fry into golden boras and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste and turmeric, and cook cubed bottle gourd covered until tender.
Add a splash of warm water, roasted cumin powder, fried fish egg boras, slit green chillies, and fresh coriander; simmer for 5 minutes.

notes: Light, comforting bottle gourd curry enriched with savory fish roe dumplings.

ingredients.name: Fresh coriander stems & leaves, finely chopped
Oil, green chilli, black pepper & salt

steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a saucepan and sauté minced garlic, ginger, chopped green chilli, and coriander stems for 1 minute.
Pour in stock, bring to a boil, and add diced vegetables and prawns. Simmer for 4-5 minutes until prawns turn pink and tender.
Stir in optional cornflour slurry, season with black pepper and salt, switch off heat, and add fresh lemon juice and coriander leaves.

notes: Light, immunity-boosting soup rich in Vitamin C and lean protein.

name: Macher Dimer Bhapa (Bengali Steamed Mustard & Coconut Fish Eggs)

ingredients.name: Fish eggs / fish roe (Hilsa, Rohu or Katla), cleaned
Yellow & black mustard seeds (soaked and ground)
White poppy seeds (posto), soaked and ground

steps.text: Grind soaked mustard seeds, poppy seeds, grated coconut, 2 green chillies, and a pinch of salt with warm water into a smooth paste.

In a steel tiffin box, fold cleaned fish roe (whole lobes or lightly pan-seared pieces) with the ground paste, whisked yogurt, turmeric, salt, and 2 tbsp raw mustard oil. Top with slit green chillies.
Close the lid tightly and steam in a covered pot with boiling water reaching halfway up the box for 18-20 minutes.

notes: Traditional Bengali tiffin-box steamed fish roe dish; serve with steaming hot white rice.

name: Macher Dimer Bharta (Bengali Smoky Mashed Fish Egg with Mustard Oil)

steps.text: Fry dry red chillies and garlic cloves in 1.5 tbsp mustard oil until crisp and golden; set aside. Pan-fry turmeric-salted fish roe covered on low heat until cooked and lightly charred.
Crush the dry red chillies and roasted garlic with salt, then mash thoroughly with the cooked fish roe.

steps.section: Fold in raw onion and mustard oil
steps.text: Mix in finely chopped raw onion, green chillies, fresh coriander leaves, and 1 tbsp pungent raw mustard oil.

notes: Smoky, fiery Bengali bharta meant to be mixed into steaming hot white rice.

name: Macher Dimer Borar Dalna (Bengali Fish Egg Fritter & Potato Dalna)

ingredients.name: Whole garam masala, cumin, coriander, Kashmiri chilli, sugar & salt

steps.section: Fry fish roe fritters and potatoes
steps.text: Whisk fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry round fritters in mustard oil. Fry potato cubes until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes and warm water; once potatoes soften, add the fish roe fritters, simmer 5 minutes, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Slightly richer than everyday jhol, with warm whole spices and a touch of ghee.

name: Macher Dimer Borar Kalia (Festive Spicy Fish Egg Fritter Kalia)

ingredients.name: Onions (1 chopped for boras, 2 grated for gravy)
Whole garam masala, Kashmiri chilli, cumin, sugar & salt

steps.text: Beat fish eggs with chopped onion, green chillies, besan, rice flour, turmeric, and salt; fry until golden and set aside.
Temper mustard oil with whole garam masala, brown the grated onions, and cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, whisked yogurt, and Kashmiri chilli powder until glossy.
Add warm water, bring to a boil, gently add the fish egg boras, and simmer for 5 minutes until plump and juicy.

notes: Plump fish egg boras absorb the rich yogurt-onion kalia gravy like sponges.

name: Macher Dimer Borar Tok (Bengali Sweet & Sour Tamarind Fish Egg Curry)

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind (tentul), soaked in warm water for pulp
Panch phoron (Bengali five-spice) & dry red chillies

steps.text: Mix fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small fritters in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper 1 tbsp mustard oil with dry red chillies and panch phoron. Pour in strained tamarind pulp, water, mustard paste, turmeric, salt, and jaggery; boil for 5 minutes.
Drop the fried fish egg boras into the tangy-sweet broth and simmer for 4 minutes until soft and juicy.

notes: Traditional Bengali summer meal-ender (tok/ambol) that cools the palate.

name: Macher Dimer Chop (Bengali Spiced Fish Egg Croquettes)

ingredients.name: Mustard oil or vegetable oil for frying

steps.text: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic, and fish roe with spices until cooked through, then mash together with boiled potatoes, crushed peanuts, bhaja masala, and coriander.
Roll into round or oval chops and coat either in breadcrumbs or a thick spiced besan batter.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown and serve hot with puffed rice (muri) or kasundi.

notes: A popular Bengali telebhaja variation for monsoon evenings.

name: Macher Dimer Cutlet (Kolkata Cabin-Style Fish Egg Cutlet)

ingredients.name: Bengali garam masala & roasted cumin-chilli powder (bhaja masala)

steps.text: Sauté minced onion, ginger, garlic, and green chillies in 1 tbsp oil, add mashed fish eggs and turmeric, and cook until dry and crumbly. Mix with mashed potato, bhaja masala, garam masala, lemon juice, and coriander.
Shape cooled mixture into flat diamond or oval cutlets, dip in cornflour or egg wash, and coat twice with breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until crisp and golden brown. Sprinkle black salt and serve with kasundi and onion salad.

notes: Crunchy Kolkata evening snack with a rich, savory fish egg center.

name: Macher Dimer Do Pyaza (Fish Egg Curry with Double Onions)

ingredients.name: Onions (1 finely chopped, 2 cut into petals)
Cumin, coriander, turmeric & Kashmiri chilli powder
Cumin seeds, dry red chilli, garam masala, coriander & salt

steps.section: Sear fish roe and onion petals
steps.text: Pan-sear seasoned fish roe slabs and cut into cubes. Toss onion petals and slit green chillies in hot oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and dry red chilli, brown chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook chopped tomatoes and spice powders.
Add the fish roe cubes, sautéed onion petals, and a splash of water; simmer for 5 minutes and finish with garam masala and coriander.

notes: Sweet, crisp-tender onion petals contrast nicely with savory fish roe.

name: Macher Dimer Kalia (Bengali Rich Fish Egg Curry)

ingredients.name: Whole garam masala, Kashmiri chilli, cumin, sugar & salt

steps.text: Steam seasoned fish roe in a greased bowl for 8 minutes, cut into neat squares, and fry lightly in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Brown grated onions, then cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, yogurt, and spices until oil floats.
Add warm water and the fish roe squares, simmer for 6 minutes, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Steaming the fish roe into a cake before cutting gives neat, firm cubes for kalia.

name: Macher Dimer Korma (Creamy Cashew & Yogurt Fish Egg Korma)

ingredients.name: Fish eggs / fish roe (steamed or fried boras)
Cashew nuts & poppy seeds (soaked and ground)
Whole garam masala, white pepper, sugar & salt

steps.text: Either pan-fry small spiced fish egg boras or lightly sear steamed fish roe cubes in ghee.
Temper ghee with cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste, then stir in whisked yogurt and cashew-poppy seed paste.
Add warm water, salt, sugar, and the fish roe pieces; simmer gently for 6 minutes and top with crushed fried onions (birista).

notes: Delicate, mildly spiced korma that pairs beautifully with pulao or paratha.

name: Macher Dimer Narkel Bora (Fish Egg & Grated Coconut Fritters)

steps.text: Mash the cleaned fish eggs in a bowl with freshly grated coconut, chopped onion, green chillies, turmeric, salt, and a tiny pinch of sugar.
Fold in besan and rice flour to form a thick, cohesive batter.
Flatten spoonfuls of the mixture in hot mustard oil and shallow-fry on medium-low heat until golden brown on both sides.

notes: Grated coconut keeps the interior of the fish egg fritters moist and subtly sweet.

name: Macher Dimer Omelette Curry (Bengali Fish Egg Omelette Dalna)

ingredients.name: Egg (beaten with fish roe for omelette) or 2 tbsp besan
Bay leaf, whole garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala & salt

steps.section: Make fish roe omelette and cut into diamonds
steps.text: Beat cleaned fish roe with 1 egg (or besan), half the chopped onion, green chillies, salt, and turmeric. Cook as a thick pancake in mustard oil on low heat, then cut into diamond pieces.
Fry potato cubes in oil, temper with bay leaf and whole spices, and sauté remaining onion, ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and ground spices.
Add warm water and cook until potatoes are soft, then gently add the fish roe omelette diamonds, simmer 5 minutes, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Cutting a thick pan-cooked fish roe omelette into diamonds creates soft, uniform pieces that hold up beautifully in gravy.

name: Macher Dimer Paturi (Banana Leaf Wrapped Mustard Fish Eggs)

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds & poppy seeds (soaked and ground)
Banana leaves (cut into squares and flame-wilted)

steps.text: Combine cleaned fish eggs with smooth mustard-poppy seed paste, grated coconut, finely chopped onion, turmeric, salt, and raw mustard oil.
Spoon portions onto oiled, flame-softened banana leaves, top each with a slit green chilli, fold into neat square parcels, and tie with cotton thread.
Cook the banana leaf parcels on a lightly oiled covered tawa over low heat for 7-8 minutes per side until the leaves char and the roe sets firm.

notes: Charred banana leaves infuse the mustard-coated fish roe with an unmistakable smoky aroma.

steps.text: Season fish with salt and turmeric, then lightly fry on both sides and set aside.
Fry potato wedges; add tomato, cumin and turmeric and sauté until fragrant.
Add water and salt, cook potatoes until nearly tender, then add fish and simmer gently.

name: Malabar Parotta (Kerala Flaky Layered Coin Parotta)

steps.text: Knead maida, sugar, salt, milk, and water for 8-10 minutes until super elastic; coat generously with oil and rest 45 minutes.
Spread each oiled ball paper-thin on a greased counter, slice into thin ribbons or gather into a long pleated rope, and coil into a pinwheel.
Pat or gently roll into a disc, cook on a hot tawa with ghee until golden, and clap between both hands to fluff the ribbon layers.

notes: Iconic South Indian flaky parotta that pairs with Kerala chemmeen roast, chicken curry, or kurma.

Heat oil, sauté the remaining chopped onion, add turmeric and Malvani masala, then stir in the ground coconut vatan and warm water.
Add cleaned prawns, kokum petals, and salt; simmer gently for 6 minutes and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Coastal Maharashtrian specialty known for its smoky roasted coconut vatan and tangy kokum.

name: Mangalorean Prawn Gassi (Yetti Gassi Coconut Red Chilli Curry)

steps.section: Roast spices and grind gassi paste

Bring the ground paste and water to a gentle boil, add cleaned prawns and salt, and simmer for 6-7 minutes.

steps.section: Temper with onions and curry leaves
steps.text: Fry finely sliced onions and curry leaves in coconut oil until crisp and golden brown, then pour over the hot curry.

notes: Pairs beautifully with neer dosa, kori rotti, or boiled red rice.

steps.text: Steam or boil shelled green peas for 5–6 minutes until tender, then drain.
Heat mustard oil, crackle cumin or nigella seeds, and sauté ginger, garlic, and green chillies with the peas for 3 minutes.
Mash or pulse into a coarse bharta, season with salt, lemon juice, and fresh coriander, and serve warm.

notes: Fresh winter green peas make a vibrant, naturally sweet and spicy bharta.

Ghee or oil, coriander leaves & salt

steps.text: Coarsely mash steamed peas and sauté in 1 tsp oil with cumin seeds, hing, crushed ginger-green chilli, amchur, garam masala, and salt until dry.
Stuff cooled green pea filling inside soft wheat dough balls and roll out evenly.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee until golden brown on both sides.

notes: Wholesome winter green pea paratha made with whole wheat flour.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, boiled and coarsely mashed by hand
Dry mango powder (amchur), red chilli, coriander, garam masala & black salt

steps.text: Heat mustard oil or ghee, temper with cumin, fennel, cloves, black pepper, and hing, then lightly roast 1 tbsp besan and ginger-green chilli paste for 1 minute.

steps.section: Simmer crushed potatoes in thin spicy broth
steps.text: Add hand-mashed potatoes, spice powders, and 2.5 cups water; simmer on low flame for 12-15 minutes.

steps.section: Finish with amchur and garam masala
steps.text: Stir in amchur powder, black salt, garam masala, and fresh coriander.

notes: Famous Mathura and Agra breakfast potato curry without onion, garlic, or tomatoes.

name: Mughlai Paratha (Kolkata Cabin-Style Egg & Spiced Keema Stuffed Paratha)

ingredients.name: Spiced cooked chicken/mutton keema or crushed breadcrumbs
Onion, ginger, garlic & green chillies, finely chopped

steps.text: Knead maida with oil, salt, and water into a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes. Beat eggs with chopped onion, green chillies, ginger, coriander, garam masala, salt, and cooked spiced keema (or breadcrumbs).

steps.section: Stretch thin and fold into envelope
steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a very thin large sheet on an oiled surface, spoon the egg-keema mixture in the center, and fold all four sides over to form a neat rectangular parcel.

Carefully slide into a flat frying pan with medium-hot oil and cook for 4-5 minutes per side until the egg sets puffily inside and the crust is golden and crisp. Cut into squares and serve with aloor torkari, ketchup, and salad.

notes: Iconic Kolkata cabin-restaurant delicacy.

name: Mulo Bharta (Radish Mash)

ingredients.name: Green chillies & roasted dry red chilli

steps.text: Peel and grate the radish, toss with a little salt, rest 5 minutes, and squeeze out the excess water.
Lightly steam or sauté the grated radish in 1 tsp mustard oil until tender and raw sharpness subsides.
Toss the warm radish with finely chopped onion, crushed roasted red chilli, green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and raw mustard oil.

notes: A popular winter Bengali side dish served with steamed rice.

ingredients.name: Instant dry yeast (or 1/2 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp baking soda)
Refined oil or ghee (for dough and deep frying)

steps.text: Activate yeast in lukewarm milk with sugar (or whisk yogurt with baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt). Knead with maida and 2 tbsp oil into a pillowy dough; cover and rest in a warm spot for 1 hour until puffed.
Divide into lemon-sized balls and roll into slightly thick rounds (thicker than regular luchi) with a sprinkle of kalonji if desired.
Slide into medium-hot oil and gently ladle hot oil over the top until each naan puri puffs into a soft, pillowy golden balloon; flip once and drain.

notes: Beloved Bengali catering & festive favorite—soft like a baby naan inside and puffed like a puri outside; pairs with chana masala or aloor dum.

name: Narkel Chingri (Prawns in Spiced Grated Coconut)

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Coarsely grind half the grated coconut with mustard seeds and 2 green chillies, keeping the rest of the grated coconut for texture.
Lightly sear turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil. Temper the oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies.
Add both the ground coconut paste and reserved grated coconut with warm water, salt, sugar, and prawns; simmer for 6-8 minutes until rich and fragrant.

notes: Uses whole freshly grated coconut for a textured, sweet-savory Bengali prawn curry.

ingredients.name: Cashew nuts & charmagaz (melon seeds), soaked and ground
Ginger paste & Kashmiri red chilli powder
Bay leaf, whole garam masala, cumin seeds, hing, sugar & salt

steps.text: Fry halved potatoes in mustard oil with a pinch of turmeric and salt until golden brown; set aside.

Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, cumin seeds, and hing. Sauté ginger paste, tomato puree, Kashmiri chilli, cumin-coriander powder, whisked yogurt, and cashew-melon seed paste until oil floats.
Add fried potatoes, warm water, salt, and a touch of sugar; cover and cook until fork-tender, finishing with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Traditional Bengali puja bhog and Ashtami luchi accompaniment without onion or garlic.

name: Notun Aloor Dum (Bengali Winter Baby Potato Dum)

ingredients.name: Baby new potatoes (notun aloo), peeled and pricked
Cumin, coriander, turmeric & Kashmiri red chilli powder
Bay leaf, whole garam masala, hing, bhaja masala, coriander & salt

steps.text: Parboil peeled baby new potatoes in salted turmeric water for 6 minutes, drain, prick with a fork, and fry in mustard oil until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, and hing. Cook ginger-green chilli paste, tomato puree, and spice powders until oil separates.

steps.section: Simmer on dum with green peas
steps.text: Add fried baby potatoes, fresh green peas, and warm water; cover and cook on low heat for 8 minutes. Finish with ghee, bhaja masala, and chopped coriander.

notes: Essential companion to Koraishutir Kochuri at every Bengali winter picnic and feast.

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves & cumin seeds (crushed into paste)

steps.text: Combine cleaned fish eggs with crushed garlic-cumin paste, chopped onion, green chillies, curry leaves, turmeric, besan, rice powder, and salt.
Shape into flat patties and pan-fry in hot mustard oil over low-medium heat until golden and cooked through.

notes: A classic Odia accompaniment to Pakhala Bhata (fermented water rice) or dalma.

name: Odia Machha Bihana Besara (Fish Eggs in Odia Mustard-Garlic Gravy)

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds, cumin & garlic cloves (ground to paste)
Tomato, chopped & ambula (dried mango) or raw mango
Besan (1.5 tbsp for roe cakes) & mustard oil

steps.section: Pan-fry fish egg cakes and potatoes
steps.text: Mix fish eggs with 1.5 tbsp besan, salt, and turmeric; pan-fry into small cakes alongside potato wedges in mustard oil.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, sauté chopped tomato, turmeric, and the ground mustard-garlic-cumin paste with warm water and potatoes.

steps.section: Add fish egg cakes and ambula
steps.text: Once potatoes are soft, add the fish egg cakes and soaked ambula, simmer 5 minutes, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Garlic-scented mustard paste (besara) and tangy ambula make this a signature Odia fish roe curry.

name: Ol Bharta (Elephant Foot Yam / Suran Chokha)

ingredients.name: Mustard paste (shorshe bata) or roasted mustard powder

steps.text: Oil your palms before peeling and cubing the elephant foot yam, then boil or pressure-cook with a slice of lemon and salt until very soft.
Drain thoroughly and mash the warm yam while hot until completely smooth.
Mix in mustard paste, chopped green chillies, lemon juice, salt, and pungent mustard oil.

notes: Lemon juice neutralizes any natural calcium oxalate itchiness in the yam and brightens the flavour.

name: Ol Chingri Dalna (Elephant Foot Yam & Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Cumin, coriander, turmeric & red chilli powder
Bay leaf, whole cumin, garam masala & salt

steps.text: Parboil cubed elephant foot yam in salted water for 5 minutes, drain, and fry until golden alongside potato cubes. Lightly fry prawns and set aside.
Temper mustard oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, cook onion and ginger-garlic paste with tomato and spice powders until oil separates.
Add yam, potatoes, and warm water; simmer until tender, then add fried prawns, garam masala, and ghee.

notes: Meaty elephant foot yam cubes soak up the spiced prawn gravy wonderfully.

name: Palak Paratha (Spiced Spinach Whole Wheat Paratha)

ingredients.name: Fresh spinach leaves (palak), blanched and pureed (or finely chopped)
Ginger, garlic & green chillies (blended with spinach)

steps.text: Blend blanched spinach with ginger, garlic, and green chillies; knead with wheat flour, besan, ajwain, salt, and 1 tsp oil into a soft green dough.
Roll each ball, brush with a drop of ghee, fold into a triangle or square, and roll out evenly.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa with ghee until cooked through and lightly browned.

notes: Iron-rich, colorful flatbread that stays soft for hours in lunchboxes.

ingredients.name: Oil or butter & 1 tbsp fresh cream
Cumin seeds, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala & salt

steps.text: Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, plunge into cold water, and blend smooth with green chillies.
Lightly sear seasoned prawns and set aside. In the same pan, crackle cumin seeds, brown chopped garlic and onion, and cook tomato with spices.
Stir in the vibrant spinach puree and seared prawns, simmer gently for 5 minutes, and finish with garam masala and a swirl of cream or butter.

notes: Iron-rich spinach and high-protein prawns make a nutritious curry for roti or rice.

steps.text: Knead wheat flour, fine sooji, ajwain, cumin, hing, salt, 1 tbsp hot oil, and spinach puree into a firm, tight poori dough; rest 15 minutes.
Roll small balls into even discs and fry in hot oil until they puff into vibrant green, crispy puris.

notes: Adding 2 tbsp fine semolina keeps Palak Puris puffed and crisp for longer.

name: Panch Phoron Aloor Torkari (Bengali Five-Spice Homestyle Potato Curry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil until smoking lightly, then temper with bay leaf, dry red chillies, and panch phoron until the seeds pop.
Add cubed potatoes, quartered tomato, slit green chillies, turmeric, and salt; stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Add warm water and a pinch of sugar, cover and cook until potatoes are soft, mash 2-3 pieces to thicken the gravy, and garnish with coriander.

notes: Simple, fragrant 5-spice Bengali potato curry that requires zero spice grinding.

steps.text: Mix maida, salt, sugar, baking soda, and 1.5 tbsp oil. Knead with lukewarm milk and water into a very soft, stretchy dough; coat with oil and rest covered for 30 minutes.

notes: Signature West Bengal street-style crushed flaky paratha traditionally served by weight with spicy ghugni or aloor torkari.

steps.text: Mix mashed fish eggs with poppy seed paste, chopped onion, green chillies, turmeric, salt, and flour.
Shape into small patties and press whole white poppy seeds onto the surface for a nutty crunch.
Fry on medium-low heat in mustard oil for 4-5 minutes per side until crisp and golden.

notes: Nutty roasted poppy seeds pair wonderfully with savory Bengali fish roe.

Temper oil with nigella seeds, fry sliced onion until soft, and stir in ground poppy seed paste with warm water.
Add the fried boras and slit green chillies, simmer gently for 5 minutes until coated in creamy posto, and drizzle with raw mustard oil.

notes: Rich, nutty poppy seed gravy with tender fish roe dumplings.

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

name: Potol Bharta (Pointed Gourd Mash)

steps.text: Lightly scrape the skin of the potol, trim the ends, and halve lengthwise.
Steam or boil the potol until tender, drain, and mash. Temper mustard oil with kalo jeere, garlic, onion, and green chilli, then stir in the mashed potol and cook until thick and fragrant.
Adjust salt, drizzle a few drops of raw mustard oil, and serve hot with steamed rice.

notes: Adding a few small fried prawns (chingri) or roasted garlic is a popular Bengali variation.

name: Potol Chingri (Pointed Gourd & Potato Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Pointed gourd (potol / parwal), scraped and halved
Cumin, coriander, turmeric & red chilli powder
Bay leaf, whole cumin, garam masala & salt

steps.text: Lightly sear seasoned prawns and remove. Fry scraped pointed gourd halves and potato wedges in mustard oil until golden brown.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, fry chopped onion until golden, and cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spices until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes, potol, and warm water; cook until tender, then stir in the prawns, simmer 4 minutes, and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: One of the most popular Bengali everyday and festive prawn-vegetable combinations.

steps.text: Wash pointed gourd peels thoroughly and boil in salted water for 5–7 minutes until soft, then drain well.
Grind the boiled peels with garlic cloves and green chillies to a smooth paste using minimal water.
Heat mustard oil, crackle kalo jeere, add the ground peel paste, salt, and a pinch of sugar, and stir-fry until dry and glossy.

notes: A classic Bengali zero-waste delicacy (Potol Khosa Bata / Bharta) served with hot steamed rice.

name: Potoler Dorma with Chingri Stuffing (Prawn-Stuffed Pointed Gourd)

ingredients.name: Large pointed gourds (potol), scraped and hollowed
Whole garam masala, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, sugar & salt

steps.text: Scrape potol skins and scoop out the seeds gently. Sauté minced prawns, scooped potol pulp, onion, ginger, grated coconut, and garam masala until dry; stuff inside each hollowed potol.
Shallow-fry the stuffed potols gently in mustard oil until golden on all sides.
Cook onion paste, tomato puree, cashew-posto paste, whisked yogurt, and spices into a velvety gravy, then nestle the stuffed potols inside and simmer gently for 7 minutes.

notes: An aristocratic Bengali culinary classic served on special occasions.

name: Prawn 65 (South Indian Spicy Deep-Fried Prawns)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli, coriander, cumin & garam masala powder
Fresh curry leaves & slit green chillies

steps.text: Mix prawns with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, red chilli powder, spices, rice flour, cornflour, and salt; rest for 15 minutes.
Fry marinated prawns in hot oil for 3 minutes until crisp and vibrant red; drain on paper towels.
In 1 tsp hot oil, crackle mustard seeds, chopped garlic, slit green chillies, and curry leaves, then toss the crispy prawns in the tempering.

notes: Crispy, fiery South Indian restaurant-style prawn starter.

name: Prawn Balchao (Goan Tangy Pickled Prawn Masala)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri dry red chillies, cumin, cloves, cinnamon & peppercorns

steps.text: Grind dry red chillies, cumin, peppercorns, cloves, cinnamon, garlic, and ginger with vinegar (no water) into a smooth fiery paste.
Quickly sear salted prawns in oil and set aside. In the same oil, fry chopped onions until deep brown and add chopped tomato.
Add the ground balchao paste, fry until oil separates, then toss in the prawns, salt, and a pinch of sugar; simmer for 5 minutes.

notes: Tangy, spicy Goan preparation inspired by Portuguese-Goan pickling traditions.

name: Prawn Bhuna (Thick Spiced Prawn Bhuna)

ingredients.name: Turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, roasted cumin & coriander powder
Curry leaves or coriander leaves, garam masala & salt

steps.text: Heat oil, temper with cumin seeds, and sauté finely chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste until rich golden brown.
Add chopped tomatoes and spice powders, roasting on medium-high heat until thick and oil separates from the sides.
Toss in the cleaned prawns and stir-fry for 5 minutes until cooked through and coated in the clinging bhuna masala. Garnish with coriander.

notes: Rich, semi-dry prawn bhuna ideal with parathas, rotis, or jeera rice.

name: Prawn Biryani (Fragrant Dum Prawn Biryani)

ingredients.name: Whole spices, saffron milk, lemon juice & salt

steps.section: Parboil basmati rice and fry birista
steps.text: Fry sliced onions in ghee and oil until crisp golden (birista). Boil soaked basmati rice with whole spices and salt until 75% cooked, then drain.
Sauté ginger-garlic paste, tomato, yogurt, biryani masala, half the birista, and herbs; add prawns and cook for just 3 minutes.
Layer the partially cooked basmati rice over the prawn masala, top with remaining birista, mint, saffron milk, and ghee, and seal on low dum heat for 10 minutes.

notes: Cooking the prawns only briefly before the final dum keeps them plump and tender.

name: Prawn Butter Masala (Creamy Tomato Butter Prawns)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli, garam masala & kasuri methi

steps.text: Season prawns with salt, turmeric, and Kashmiri chilli; sear in 1 tbsp butter for 2 minutes and set aside.
Melt remaining butter, sauté ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, Kashmiri chilli powder, and cashew paste until rich and glossy.
Add warm water, salt, a pinch of sugar, and the seared prawns. Simmer 4 minutes, then stir in fresh cream and crushed kasuri methi.

notes: Velvety, mildly spiced restaurant-style butter masala that pairs great with butter naan or pulao.

name: Prawn Caldine (Goan Mild Yellow Coconut Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Thick & thin coconut milk (or 1 cup grated coconut)
Coriander seeds, cumin, turmeric, garlic & black pepper

steps.text: Grind coriander seeds, cumin, turmeric, peppercorns, and garlic with thin coconut milk into a smooth golden paste.
Sauté sliced onion and chopped tomato in oil until soft, then add the ground yellow paste and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.section: Add prawns and thick coconut milk
steps.text: Add cleaned prawns, slit green chillies, tamarind, and thick coconut milk; simmer gently for 6 minutes until cooked through.

notes: A gentle, aromatic Goan curry without red chillies, getting its gentle warmth from green chillies and black pepper.

name: Prawn Curry (Homestyle Indian Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Turmeric, cumin, coriander & red chilli powder
Whole spices, garam masala, coriander leaves & salt

steps.text: Toss cleaned prawns with salt and turmeric; lightly sear in oil for 1-2 minutes and set aside.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf, brown the chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste, and cook tomatoes with spice powders until oil separates.
Add warm water to reach desired gravy consistency, return the prawns, simmer for 5 minutes, and garnish with garam masala and fresh coriander.

notes: Classic everyday Indian prawn curry suitable for both lunch and dinner.

name: Prawn Cutlet (Kolkata Cabin-Style Chingri Cutlet)

ingredients.name: Jumbo or large prawns (peeled, tail on, butterflied flat)
Ginger, garlic, green chilli & coriander paste
Fresh lemon juice & crushed black pepper

steps.text: Slit large prawns down the back and gently flatten them into cutlets while keeping the tail intact. Marinate with ginger-garlic-green chilli paste, lemon juice, black pepper, and salt for 15 minutes.
Dust each butterflied prawn in flour, dip into beaten egg, and press firmly into breadcrumbs twice for a crisp crust.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Sprinkle with black salt and serve with kasundi and salad.

notes: Signature heritage Kolkata cabin-style prawn cutlet.

name: Prawn Do Pyaza (Prawns with Double Onions)

ingredients.name: Onions (1 finely chopped, 2 cut into petals)
Cumin, coriander, turmeric & Kashmiri chilli powder
Whole spices, dry red chilli, garam masala, coriander & salt

steps.text: Quickly toss onion petals and slit green chillies in hot oil for 2 minutes until glossy and crisp-tender; set aside with lightly seared prawns.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and whole dry red chilli, fry finely chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook chopped tomatoes and spice powders.
Add prawns, sautéed onion petals, and a splash of water; simmer for 5 minutes and finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.

notes: Uses onions in two stages for both a rich gravy base and sweet, crunchy onion petals.

name: Prawn Fried Rice (Indo-Chinese Wok-Tossed Shrimp Fried Rice)

ingredients.name: Prawns (small or medium, peeled and deveined)
Carrot, French beans & capsicum, finely diced

steps.text: Heat oil in a wok, stir-fry seasoned prawns for 2 minutes until pink, push aside or remove, and scramble the beaten eggs.
On high flame, stir-fry minced garlic, spring onion whites, finely diced carrots, beans, and capsicum for 2-3 minutes so they stay crisp.
Add cold cooked rice, prawns, scrambled egg, soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper, and salt; toss on high heat and finish with spring onion greens.

notes: Day-old or thoroughly chilled rice gives the best non-sticky restaurant wok texture.

name: Prawn Fry (Chingri Macher Bhaja / Masala Prawn Fry)

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder & Kashmiri red chilli powder
Curry leaves or sliced onion & salt

steps.text: Rub cleaned prawns with turmeric, red chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, black pepper, lemon juice, and salt; rest for 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a skillet until smoking lightly, arrange prawns in a single layer, and fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crisp on the outside.

notes: Simple, flavorful pan-fried prawns that pair perfectly with dal and steamed rice.

name: Prawn Ghee Roast (Mangalorean Kundapur Prawn Ghee Roast)

ingredients.name: Coriander seeds, cumin, fenugreek & black pepper

steps.text: Marinate prawns with yogurt, turmeric, lemon juice, and salt. Dry-roast Byadgi chillies, coriander, cumin, fenugreek, and pepper; grind smooth with garlic and tamarind.
Heat 1.5 tbsp ghee, sear marinated prawns on high heat for 2 minutes, and remove.
In the remaining ghee, slow-roast the ground chilli-garlic paste until dark red and ghee separates, then fold in the prawns, a pinch of jaggery, and crisp curry leaves.

notes: Iconic Kundapur Mangalorean delicacy famous for its rich ghee aroma and fiery-tangy glaze.

name: Prawn Hakka Noodles (Stir-Fried Shrimp Chowmein)

ingredients.name: Soy sauce, green chilli sauce & rice vinegar

steps.text: Boil Hakka noodles until al dente, rinse in cold water, and toss with 1 tsp oil. Stir-fry seasoned prawns in hot oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok, sauté garlic, ginger, and sliced onion, then toss julienned cabbage, carrot, and bell pepper on high heat for 2 minutes.
Add boiled noodles, seared prawns, soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, black pepper, and spring onion greens; toss well.

notes: Street-style Kolkata prawn chowmein great as an evening meal or dinner.

name: Prawn in Yogurt Curry (Doi Chingri)

ingredients.name: Whole garam masala, turmeric, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Rub prawns with a pinch of salt and turmeric, sear lightly in hot oil for 1 minute per side, and set aside.
Temper oil with cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf. Cook onion paste and ginger-garlic paste on low heat until raw aroma disappears.
Lower the flame, stir in whisked yogurt mixed with a pinch of flour or cashew paste to prevent curdling, add warm water, prawns, and slit green chillies, and simmer gently for 6-8 minutes.

notes: Always beat the yogurt until velvety and add it over low heat so the gravy stays silky.

name: Prawn Jalfrezi (Stir-Fried Prawns with Peppers & Tomatoes)

ingredients.name: Green, yellow or red bell peppers, cut into strips
Cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder & vinegar

steps.text: Sear seasoned prawns for 2 minutes and remove. Stir-fry onion strips and bell peppers on high heat for 2 minutes so they stay crunchy.
Sauté garlic paste, ginger juliennes, tomato puree, and spice powders with a splash of vinegar or ketchup until thick.
Return prawns, crisp peppers, onions, and fresh tomato wedges to the pan; toss for 3 minutes and garnish with coriander.

notes: Colorful, semi-dry Anglo-Indian prawn stir-fry.

name: Prawn Koliwada (Mumbai Style Crispy Fried Prawns)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli, roasted cumin & chaat masala

steps.text: Rub prawns with lemon juice, ginger-garlic-chilli paste, turmeric, and salt; rest for 10 minutes.
Mix besan, cornflour, yogurt, carom seeds, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and cumin powder into a thick paste and coat the prawns.

steps.section: Deep-fry and dust with chaat masala
steps.text: Deep-fry in hot oil for 3 minutes until crunchy. Sprinkle generously with chaat masala and serve with mint-coriander chutney.

notes: Carom seeds (ajwain) and chaat masala give Prawn Koliwada its unmistakable Mumbai seafood punch.

name: Prawn Korma (Creamy Cashew & Yogurt Prawn Korma)

ingredients.name: Onions (fried golden and ground with yogurt)
Cashew nuts & melon/poppy seeds (soaked and ground)
Whole garam masala, coriander powder, white pepper & salt

steps.section: Sear prawns and prepare korma paste
steps.text: Lightly sear prawns in ghee for 1-2 minutes. Blend fried golden onions with yogurt and soaked cashews into a silky paste.
Temper ghee with cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and bay leaf; sauté ginger-garlic paste and coriander powder until fragrant.
Stir in the onion-yogurt-cashew paste and warm water, simmer for 5 minutes, then add prawns and cook gently for 5 minutes.

notes: Mild, luxurious prawn curry ideal for guests and festive dinners.

name: Prawn Manchow Soup (Spicy Indo-Chinese Shrimp Soup)

ingredients.name: Cabbage, carrot, beans & mushrooms, finely chopped
Garlic, ginger & green chillies, finely minced
Fresh coriander stems & spring onions, chopped

steps.text: Heat oil in a pot, sauté minced garlic, ginger, green chillies, and coriander stems on high heat, then toss in chopped prawns and vegetables for 2 minutes.
Pour in 3 cups water or stock, soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, black pepper, and salt; bring to a rolling boil.

steps.section: Thicken and top with crispy noodles
steps.text: Stir in the cornflour slurry until glossy and lightly thickened. Garnish with spring onions and crunchy fried noodles.

notes: Hearty, warming Indo-Chinese soup.

name: Prawn Masala (Spicy Onion-Tomato Prawn Masala)

ingredients.name: Turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli, coriander & cumin powder
Green chillies, garam masala, lemon juice, coriander & salt

steps.text: Marinate cleaned prawns with turmeric, half the chilli powder, lemon juice, and salt for 10 minutes.
Heat oil, fry chopped onions until golden brown, add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and remaining spice powders, and cook until oil separates.
Add marinated prawns and slit green chillies, cook covered for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender, and finish with garam masala and fresh coriander.

notes: Versatile Indian prawn masala that goes equally well with steamed rice, roti, or parotta.

name: Prawn Mayo Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Prawn Omelette (Masala Chingri Dim Omelette)

steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a skillet and sauté chopped prawns with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 2-3 minutes until cooked through.
Beat the eggs aggressively with chopped onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, black pepper, salt, and the cooked prawns.
Pour into the hot oiled skillet, cook on medium-low heat until set underneath, flip gently, and cook until golden on both sides.

notes: High-protein breakfast or quick dinner side dish.

name: Prawn Pakora (Crispy Chingri Pakora)

ingredients.name: Red chilli powder, lemon juice & salt
Mustard oil or vegetable oil for frying

steps.text: Pat dry the cleaned prawns and toss with lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt. Rest for 10 minutes.
Whisk besan, rice flour, carom seeds, chopped green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and cold water into a thick, smooth coating batter.
Dip each marinated prawn into the batter and fry in medium-hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden and crisp. Serve hot with kasundi or mint chutney.

notes: Adding rice flour keeps the pakora crust crisp; do not overcook prawns so they stay juicy inside.

name: Prawn Pepper Fry (South Indian Milagu Eral Varuval)

ingredients.name: Freshly crushed black peppercorns & fennel seeds

steps.text: Toast whole black peppercorns, fennel seeds, and cumin seeds briefly, then crush coarsely in a mortar and pestle.
Heat coconut oil, crackle curry leaves, and fry crushed ginger-garlic and sliced shallots until golden.
Add cleaned prawns, turmeric, and salt; cook for 5 minutes until moisture dries up, then coat with the crushed pepper-fennel masala and lemon juice.

notes: Bold, aromatic black pepper prawn dry fry great as a starter or side with sambar/rasam rice.

name: Prawn Potato Curry (Aloo Chingri Jhol)

ingredients.name: Cumin, coriander, turmeric & red chilli powder
Cumin seeds, bay leaf, garam masala & salt

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric; lightly fry in mustard oil for 1-2 minutes and remove. In the same oil, fry potato wedges until golden.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf. Sauté sliced onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders with a splash of water.
Add fried potatoes and warm water; cover and cook until potatoes are tender. Stir in the prawns, simmer for 4 minutes, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Classic everyday Bengali and eastern Indian prawn potato curry served with steamed rice.

name: Prawn Pulao (Spiced Basmati Prawn Pilaf)

ingredients.name: Whole garam masala, turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala & salt

steps.text: Heat ghee and oil, temper with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and shahi jeera. Fry sliced onions until golden, then sauté ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spices.
Stir in cleaned prawns, mint, and coriander leaves; sauté for 2 minutes, then gently fold in the drained basmati rice.
Pour in 2.75 cups warm water or stock, season with salt, cover tightly, and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes until grains are fluffy.

notes: One-pot fragrant prawn rice meal.

name: Prawn Rezala (Bengali Mughlai White Yogurt & Cashew Gravy)

ingredients.name: Cashew nuts & white poppy seeds (soaked and ground)
Whole white spices, dry red chillies, kewra water, sugar & salt

steps.text: Toss prawns with salt and white pepper, sear lightly in ghee for 1 minute without browning, and set aside.
Temper ghee with bay leaf, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and whole dry red chillies. Cook boiled onion paste and ginger-garlic paste on low heat.

steps.section: Simmer with yogurt and cashew paste
steps.text: Add whisked yogurt and cashew-poppy seed paste, pour in warm water, add prawns, white pepper, salt, sugar, and a drop of kewra water; simmer gently for 6 minutes.

notes: Silky, ivory-white Kolkata Mughlai gravy that pairs wonderfully with roomali roti, parotta, or pulao.

name: Prawn Salad (Fresh Citrus, Cucumber & Herb Prawn Salad)

ingredients.name: Cucumber, cherry tomatoes & bell pepper, diced
Garlic, black pepper, chilli flakes, herbs & salt

steps.text: Sear seasoned prawns in 1 tsp olive oil with garlic and black pepper for 2 minutes per side until pink, then cool slightly.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, honey, chilli flakes, salt, and chopped herbs into a bright vinaigrette.
Toss crisp greens, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, and warm or chilled prawns with the dressing just before serving.

notes: Light, refreshing, protein-packed meal.

name: Prawn Skewers (Tawa Grilled Spiced Prawn Skewers)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chilli, roasted cumin, coriander & garam masala

steps.text: Toss prawns, cubed bell peppers, and onion petals with ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, spice powders, oil, and salt; rest for 15 minutes.
Alternate marinated prawns, bell peppers, and onions on wooden or metal skewers.
Cook on a hot cast-iron tawa or grill pan with a brush of butter for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly charred; sprinkle with chaat masala.

notes: Party starter that cooks quickly on any flat tawa or grill pan.

name: Prawn Tempura (Light Crispy Batter-Fried Shrimp)

ingredients.name: Large prawns (peeled, tail on, scored along the belly)
Egg (lightly beaten) or 1/2 tsp baking soda
Ice-cold sparkling water or ice water
White pepper, soy dipping sauce & salt

steps.text: Make 3 small shallow cuts across the underside of each prawn so it stays straight while frying, pat completely dry, and dust lightly with flour.
Briefly stir ice-cold water, beaten egg, flour, and cornstarch together with chopsticks, leaving a few small lumps so the batter stays airy.
Dip prawns into the cold batter and fry in 180°C oil for 2-3 minutes until pale golden and shatteringly crisp.

notes: Keeping the batter ice-cold and minimally mixed guarantees a light, lacy tempura crust.

name: Prawn Tikka Masala (Chargrilled Prawns in Spiced Tomato Gravy)

ingredients.name: Thick yogurt, besan & lemon juice (for tikka marinade)
Kashmiri chilli, tandoori masala, kasuri methi & salt

steps.text: Coat prawns in thick yogurt, roasted besan, ginger-garlic, tandoori masala, and lemon juice; pan-grill on high heat until lightly charred.
Sauté chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste in butter and oil until golden, then cook tomato puree and spices until thick and glossy.

steps.section: Simmer with cream and kasuri methi
steps.text: Add warm water, chargrilled prawns, fresh cream, and crushed kasuri methi; simmer together for 3 minutes.

notes: Combines smoky tandoori prawns with a rich North Indian tomato-cream gravy.

name: Prawn Vindaloo (Goan Garlic & Vinegar Spicy Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Cumin seeds, peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves & mustard seeds
Toddy vinegar or apple cider vinegar

steps.text: Soak dry red chillies and spices in vinegar, then grind with garlic and ginger into a smooth, vibrant red vindaloo paste.
Heat oil, fry chopped onions until golden, add the vindaloo paste, and roast until oil separates. Add parboiled potato cubes and warm water.
Add cleaned prawns, salt, and a pinch of jaggery; simmer for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender.

notes: Authentic Goan vindaloo relies on garlic, warm whole spices, and vinegar without dairy.

name: Prawn Xacuti (Goan Roasted Spice, Poppy Seed & Coconut Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chillies, coriander seeds, cloves, cinnamon, star anise & nutmeg
Onions (1 sliced for roasting, 1 finely chopped)

steps.text: Dry-roast whole spices, red chillies, poppy seeds, sliced onion, and grated coconut until golden brown; grind with garlic, turmeric, and tamarind into a smooth, fragrant paste.
Heat coconut oil, sauté finely chopped onion until soft, add the ground Xacuti masala paste and water, and simmer for 6 minutes.
Add cleaned prawns and salt, simmer gently for 5-6 minutes until cooked through, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Complex, deeply aromatic Goan curry featuring toasted coconut, poppy seeds, and warm spices.

name: Pudina Lachha Paratha (Mint Layered Flaky Paratha)

ingredients.name: Dried crushed mint leaves (pudina powder) & fresh chopped mint

steps.section: Roll and layer with mint & ghee
steps.text: Roll kneaded wheat dough into a thin circle, brush with ghee, and sprinkle crushed mint leaves, chaat masala, and cumin powder.
Fold into accordion pleats, coil tightly, press flat, and roll into a medium circle.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and aromatic.

notes: Refreshing mint-scented multi-layered paratha.

name: Pui Shak Diye Macher Dimer Chorchori (Malabar Spinach, Pumpkin & Fish Egg Medley)

ingredients.name: Malabar spinach leaves & stems (pui shak), chopped
Turmeric, cumin powder, green chillies, sugar & salt

steps.text: Pan-fry turmeric-salted fish roe in mustard oil until firm, break into bite-sized pieces, and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron, dry red chilli, crushed garlic, and sliced onion. Add potato, pumpkin, pui shak stems and leaves, turmeric, cumin powder, and salt; cover and cook until tender.
Stir in the fried fish roe pieces, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered for 5 minutes until thick and cohesive.

notes: Rustic Bengali monsoon favorite combining leafy greens and sweet pumpkin with fish eggs.

name: Pui Shak Kumro Chingri Chorchori (Malabar Spinach & Pumpkin with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Malabar spinach leaves & tender stems (pui shak), chopped
Panch phoron (Bengali five-spice) & dry red chilli
Turmeric, green chillies, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil and remove. Fry potato, pumpkin, and brinjal cubes for 3 minutes.
Temper oil with panch phoron, dry red chilli, and bay leaf. Add pui shak stems and leaves, vegetables, ginger paste, turmeric, and salt; cover and cook until tender.
Stir in the fried prawns, mustard paste, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered for 5 minutes until cohesive.

notes: Classic Bengali monsoon and summer chorchori.

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal & chana dal
Fresh curry leaves, grated ginger & chopped green chillies
Fresh lemon juice, coriander leaves, pinch of sugar & salt

steps.text: Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal, and chana dal until golden, then add hing, curry leaves, ginger, and green chillies.
Add sliced onions and turmeric powder; sauté until soft and translucent without browning.
Add boiled potatoes, salt, a pinch of sugar, and 1/2 cup warm water; mash slightly and cook covered for 5 minutes. Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.

notes: Classic golden potato bhaji served with hot puffed pooris or dosa.

ingredients.name: Onions, very finely chopped and squeezed dry

steps.text: Toss finely chopped onions with roasted besan, green chillies, coriander, ajwain, crushed coriander seeds, amchur, red chilli powder, and add salt right before stuffing.
Place the spiced onion mixture inside rolled wheat dough cups, seal tightly, and roll out gently.
Pan-fry on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and golden brown on both sides.

notes: Adding 1 tbsp roasted besan prevents the onions from releasing water while rolling.

name: Radhaballabhi (Bengali Spiced Urad Dal Stuffed Puri)

ingredients.name: Split black gram (biuli / urad dal), soaked 3 hours
Fennel seeds (mouri), cumin seeds & dry red chilli (roasted and ground)

steps.text: Grind soaked urad dal with green chillies and ginger into a coarse paste. Temper oil with hing and nigella seeds, sauté the dal paste with roasted fennel-cumin masala, salt, and sugar until dry and aromatic; cool completely.
Knead flour with ghee, salt, and water into a smooth dough. Stuff each dough ball with a portion of spiced urad dal paste, seal tightly, and roll into medium-thick rounds.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides. Serve hot with cholar dal or aloor dum.

notes: Iconic Bengali festive stuffed puri scented with roasted fennel (mouri), ginger, and hing.

name: Rava Fish Egg Fry (Konkani Semolina-Crusted Fish Roe Fry)

steps.text: Cut firm fish roe into thick slabs and marinate with tamarind or kokum extract, red chilli powder, turmeric, a pinch of hing, and salt for 10 minutes.

steps.section: Crust in rava and rice flour
steps.text: Mix fine semolina and rice flour on a plate and press each marinated roe slice firmly into the mixture.
Shallow-fry on medium-low heat in coconut oil for 4 minutes per side until golden and crunchy.

notes: Traditional Goan and Malvani coastal fish roe fry (Gabholi Rava Fry).

name: Rava Prawn Fry (Crispy Semolina-Crusted Prawns)

ingredients.name: Large or medium prawns, cleaned and deveined
Ginger-garlic paste & tamarind pulp or lemon juice
Kashmiri red chilli, turmeric & coriander powder
Coconut oil or vegetable oil for shallow frying

steps.section: Coat prawns in tangy spice paste
steps.text: Mix ginger-garlic paste, tamarind or lemon juice, red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt; rub thoroughly over the prawns and rest 15 minutes.

steps.section: Dredge in semolina and rice flour
steps.text: Combine fine rava and rice flour on a plate with a pinch of salt and press each spiced prawn into the mixture so it is evenly crusted.
Shallow-fry on a hot tawa or skillet with oil for 2-3 minutes per side until the semolina crust turns golden and crisp.

notes: Goan and Karwar coastal favorite with a super-crunchy golden semolina crust.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps.section: Temper oil with kalo jeere and green chillies
steps.text: Heat oil in a kadai and temper with nigella seeds (kalo jeere), a pinch of hing, and 2 slit green chillies until fragrant.
Add the small potato cubes and salt (do not add turmeric or red chilli powder so the curry stays ivory-white); stir-fry on medium heat for 3-4 minutes.

steps.section: Simmer and lightly mash for creamy broth
steps.text: Pour in warm water, cover and cook until potatoes are soft, then mash a few potato cubes against the side of the pan with your ladle to thicken the white broth. Add sugar and remaining green chillies.

notes: Signature Bengali no-turmeric, no-onion-garlic white potato curry classically paired with hot phulko luchi or trikon porota for breakfast.

name: Sajne Data Aloo Chingri Chorchori (Drumstick, Potato & Prawn Medley)

ingredients.name: Drumsticks (sajne data), peeled and cut into 2.5-inch batons

steps.text: Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil and set aside. Temper oil with nigella seeds and fry potato wedges for 3 minutes.
Add drumstick batons, chopped tomato, turmeric, salt, and warm water; cover and cook until potatoes and drumsticks are tender.

steps.section: Finish with mustard paste and prawns
steps.text: Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, and mustard paste; simmer for 4 minutes and drizzle with raw mustard oil.

notes: Springtime Bengali delicacy combining tender moringa drumsticks with mustard and prawns.

name: Sajne Data Bharta (Drumstick / Moringa Pod Pulp Mash)

steps.text: Cut drumsticks into 3-inch pieces and boil in salted water until soft.
Split the boiled drumsticks and scrape out the soft inner pulp and tender seeds with a spoon, discarding the woody outer fibres.
Mash the drumstick pulp with mustard paste, finely chopped onion, crushed green chillies, salt, and raw mustard oil.

notes: Nutrient-dense seasonal spring bharta popular in Bengal.

name: Sajne Phool Diye Macher Dimer Bora (Drumstick Blossom & Fish Egg Fritters)

ingredients.name: Drumstick blossoms (sajne phool), washed and drained

steps.text: Gently wash moringa blossoms, squeeze out excess water, and mix with mashed fish eggs, chopped onion, green chillies, nigella seeds, turmeric, salt, besan, and rice flour.
Shape into small flat patties and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil over medium-low heat until crisp and golden on both sides.

notes: Seasonal early-spring Bengali specialty combining nutrient-rich moringa flowers with fish roe.

name: Sattu Paratha (Bihari Spiced Roasted Gram Flour Stuffed Paratha)

ingredients.name: Onion, garlic, ginger & green chillies, finely minced
Mustard oil & tangy mango pickle masala (achar masala)
Fresh lemon juice & chopped coriander leaves
Ghee or mustard oil (for roasting) & salt

steps.text: Combine sattu with minced onion, garlic, ginger, green chillies, coriander, ajwain, kalonji, mustard oil, mango pickle masala, lemon juice, salt, and a splash of water into a crumbly filling.
Form a cup in each whole wheat dough ball, pack generously with the spiced sattu mixture, seal, and roll into medium-thick circles.
Cook on a hot iron tawa with mustard oil or ghee on both sides until golden brown. Serve with baingan bharta, aloo chokha, and curd.

notes: High-protein Bihari and eastern Indian staple known as Makuni or Chatu Porota.

name: Sattu Puri (Bihari Spiced Roasted Gram Flour Stuffed Poori)

ingredients.name: Carom seeds (ajwain), kalonji, minced garlic, ginger & green chilli
Mustard oil & lemon juice / pickle masala

steps.text: Mix sattu with ajwain, kalonji, minced garlic, ginger, green chilli, mustard oil, pickle masala, lemon juice, and salt.
Seal a spoonful of sattu filling inside each dough ball, flatten and roll gently into small discs, and deep-fry in medium-hot oil until puffed and golden.

notes: Travels well and pairs with aloo dum, baingan chokha, or mango pickle.

name: Schezwan Prawns (Fiery Indo-Chinese Stir-Fried Prawns)

ingredients.name: Oil, soy sauce, vinegar & pinch of sugar

steps.text: Coat prawns in cornflour, flour, salt, and pepper; fry in hot oil until golden and crisp.
In a hot wok, stir-fry minced garlic, ginger, diced onions, and bell peppers for 2 minutes, then add Schezwan sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, and a splash of water.
Toss the crispy prawns into the glossy Schezwan glaze and garnish with spring onion greens.

notes: Bold, spicy, and garlicky prawn appetizer or main dish.

name: Schezwan Veg Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

name: Shim Bharta (Flat Beans Mash)

steps.text: Trim ends and side strings from the flat beans, wash well, and boil with a pinch of salt until soft. Drain completely.
Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere, garlic, and chillies, add the boiled shim to dry off moisture, then mash or grind smoothly.
Fold in finely chopped raw onion, fresh coriander leaves, and a drizzle of mustard oil.

notes: A beloved winter Bengali delicacy.

name: Shorshe Chingri (Prawns in Bengali Mustard Gravy)

ingredients.name: Yellow & black mustard seeds (soaked and ground)

steps.text: Grind soaked mustard seeds and poppy seeds with 2 green chillies, a pinch of salt, and warm water into a silky paste.
Rub prawns with turmeric and salt, sear in hot mustard oil for 1 minute per side, and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, pour in the mustard paste mixed with warm water, add prawns, and simmer for 5 minutes. Finish with 1 tbsp raw mustard oil.

notes: Pungent, classic Bengali mustard prawn curry that takes just 15 minutes to cook.

name: Shorshe Diye Macher Dimer Borar Jhal (Fish Egg Fritters in Mustard Gravy)

ingredients.name: Yellow & black mustard seeds (soaked and ground)

steps.text: Combine fish roe, chopped onion, green chillies, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry into golden fritters.
Temper mustard oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, sauté chopped tomato with turmeric, and pour in the mustard paste mixed with warm water.
Add the fish egg boras, simmer for 4-5 minutes, and finish with chopped coriander and a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Sharp Bengali mustard gravy pairs wonderfully with savory fish roe fritters.

name: Shorshe Macher Dim (Fish Eggs in Bengali Mustard Gravy)

ingredients.name: Fish eggs / fish roe sacs, cleaned
Mustard seeds (soaked and ground with green chillies)

steps.text: Rub fish roe sacs with salt and turmeric, sear gently in mustard oil until firm on both sides, and cut into thick slices.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, add turmeric, chilli powder, and strained mustard paste with warm water.
Add the seared fish roe slices, simmer on low heat for 5 minutes, and drizzle 1 tbsp raw mustard oil before serving.

notes: Quick 25-minute Bengali mustard fish roe curry.

Add the poached fish roe pieces and freshly crushed black pepper-cumin masala; toss on medium-low heat for 6 minutes and garnish with coriander.

steps.text: Knead flour with warm reduced sugar palm pulp, sugar, fennel seeds, a pinch of salt, and 1 tbsp ghee into a smooth golden dough.
Roll into small rounds and deep-fry in medium-hot oil until puffed and golden.

notes: Traditional Bengali Janmashtami and monsoon delicacy made with ripe palm fruit (taal).

ingredients.name: Jumbo or tiger prawns, cleaned and deveined
Kashmiri red chilli, tandoori masala, roasted cumin & chaat masala

steps.text: Whisk hung curd, warm mustard oil, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli, tandoori masala, ajwain, kasuri methi, lemon juice, and salt; coat the prawns and marinate for 20 minutes.
Thread prawns onto skewers and roast in a high-heat oven/air-fryer at 200°C or on a cast-iron grill pan for 3-4 minutes per side, basting with butter.
Dust with chaat masala and serve hot with mint-yogurt chutney and onion rings.

notes: Smoky, succulent North Indian starter that cooks in minutes.

steps.text: Simmer the whole fish roe sacs gently in salted turmeric water for 5 minutes until firm, cool, and cut into thick slices.

Pan-fry on a cast-iron tawa with oil and curry leaves for 3 minutes per side until a charred, spicy crust forms.

notes: Poaching the roe briefly first keeps the slices neat and firm for tawa frying.

name: Trikon Porota (Bengali Triangular Layered Paratha)

steps.text: Combine atta and maida with salt, a pinch of sugar, 1 tbsp oil, and warm water; knead until soft and rest for 15 minutes.
Roll each ball into a circle, brush with oil/ghee, fold in half into a semicircle, brush again, and fold in half into a triangle; roll evenly into a three-cornered paratha.
Cook on a hot tawa until brown spots appear, then drizzle ghee or oil around the edges and press gently until all three layers puff up.

notes: Classic Bengali homestyle 3-cornered breakfast paratha served with aloor chokka or Fried Egg.

Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

name: Ucche Aloo Bharta (Bitter Gourd & Potato Mash)

steps.text: Wash ucche, discard tough seeds if mature, and cut ucche and peeled potatoes into medium cubes.
Boil or steam the potatoes and ucche with a pinch of salt until soft and dry off any remaining water in the pan.
Mash warm ucche and potato together with chopped green chillies, salt, and raw mustard oil. Serve as a traditional Bengali first-course starter with hot rice.

notes: Traditionally eaten at the start of a Bengali lunch with hot steamed rice (gorom bhaat).

name: Ucche Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Chorchori (Bitter Gourd, Potato & Fish Egg Medley)

steps.section: Fry bitter gourd and fish roe
steps.text: Fry bitter gourd slices in mustard oil until golden. Lightly fry seasoned fish roe and break into coarse chunks.
Temper oil with panch phoron and green chillies, sauté sliced onion and potato wedges with turmeric and salt until nearly soft.

steps.section: Braise with fish roe and mustard
steps.text: Add fried bitter gourd, fish roe chunks, mustard paste, and a splash of water; cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.

notes: Traditional Bengali lunch opener balancing bitter ucche with rich fish roe.

name: Ukadiche Modak

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.
